definition_zh: 抵押物；抵押品；附带的；并行的
definition_en: property pledged as security for a debt; running side by side, parallel
core_image: 一个保险箱里塞满了金条和房产证，保险箱的钥匙挂在银行的门框上
scene: 一位创业者拿着一份专利申请走进银行，希望用它做担保换一笔启动资金。 The bank accepted the patent as collateral for the loan.
sceneCN: 这里 collateral 指「贷款抵押品」（第 3 个义项：为债务担保而抵押的财产）；句意为银行接受了这项专利作为贷款的抵押品。图中可辨识物件：专利证书、贷款合同、保险箱。

pos.zh: 抵押品（不可数；可数时指多项）

senses.title: side by side
senses.definition: running along the side of something; parallel
senses.definitionCN: 沿着某物的一侧延伸的；平行的
senses.example: A collateral vein runs beside the main river.
senses.exampleCN: 一条并行的支流沿着主河道流淌。
senses.why: The root means 'side', so the first sense is literal position.
senses.whyCN: 词根的意思是「侧面」，所以第一个义项是字面位置。

senses.title: accompanying, secondary
senses.definition: accompanying but secondary to something else
senses.definitionCN: 伴随着但居次要地位的
senses.example: Collateral benefits came from the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 合并带来了附带利益。
senses.why: What sits beside something is secondary to the main thing.
senses.whyCN: 坐在旁边的东西是主要事物的次要伴随物。

senses.title: security for a debt
senses.definition: property pledged to guarantee repayment of a loan
senses.definitionCN: 为保证贷款偿还而质押的财产
senses.example: Start-ups often lack collateral for bank loans.
senses.exampleCN: 初创公司往往没有抵押品来申请银行贷款。
senses.why: This is the financial borrowing of the 'sitting beside' idea: property sits beside the loan as its guarantee.
senses.whyCN: 这是金融上对「坐旁边」想法的借用：财产坐在贷款旁边作担保。

senses.title: side issue
senses.definition: a matter accompanying but separate from the main issue
senses.definitionCN: 伴随但独立于主要问题的一件事
senses.example: Collateral questions delayed the hearing.
senses.exampleCN: 一些次要问题延迟了听证。
senses.why: Another extension of 'sitting beside' the main thing.
senses.whyCN: 另一种「坐在主要事物旁边」的延伸。

senses.title: cross-connected vessels
senses.definition: connected through side paths, especially of blood vessels
senses.definitionCN: 通过侧支连接的，尤指血管
senses.example: Collateral vessels supplied blood around the blockage.
senses.exampleCN: 侧支血管绕开堵塞为组织供血。
senses.why: Medicine borrowed the 'side' sense for vessels that run beside the main path.
senses.whyCN: 医学借用「侧面」义来指沿着主要通路旁边走的血管。

senses.title: collateral damage
senses.definition: harm to bystanders from a military or political action
senses.definitionCN: 军事或政治行动中给旁观者造成的伤害
senses.example: Strikes risk heavy collateral damage in crowded cities.
senses.exampleCN: 在拥挤城市空袭可能造成严重附带损害。
senses.why: The damage sits beside the intended target.
senses.whyCN: 这种损害发生在瞄准目标的旁边。

senses.title: additional evidence
senses.definition: evidence that supports but does not directly prove
senses.definitionCN: 能支持但不能直接证明的证据
senses.example: The letter provided collateral for the witness's claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信为证人的主张提供了旁证。
senses.why: Evidence that sits beside the main case.
senses.whyCN: 坐在主要案件旁边的证据。

senses.title: network of backups
senses.definition: interconnected backup channels in a network
senses.definitionCN: 网络中互相连接的备用通道
senses.example: The internet relies on collateral links to survive outages.
senses.exampleCN: 互联网靠备用链路挺过中断。
senses.why: Side channels that run beside the main ones.
senses.whyCN: 沿着主通道旁边走的侧面通道。

intro.en: Collateral comes from Latin lateralis 'of the side', with col- 'together' added. Literally 'alongside'.
intro.cn: collateral 来自拉丁语 lateralis「侧面的」，前面加了 col-「一起」。字面意思是「沿旁边走」。

items.en: Latin latus 'side, flank' gave lateralis 'of the side'.
items.cn: 拉丁语 latus「侧面、胁部」产生 lateralis「侧面的」。

items.en: The prefix col- (a form of com- 'together') was added, making collateralis 'running alongside'.
items.cn: 加上前缀 col-（com-「一起」的一种形式），变成 collateralis「沿旁边一起走的」。

items.en: The adjective entered English in the 15th century meaning 'side by side, parallel'.
items.cn: 这个形容词于 15 世纪进入英语，意为「并排的、平行的」。

items.en: The financial noun meaning 'security for a loan' appeared in legal writing by the 17th century.
items.cn: 财务名词义「贷款担保」见于 17 世纪法律文书。

items.en: The phrase collateral damage emerged in military jargon around the 1950s and broadened after 2001.
items.cn: collateral damage 这个说法 1950 年代见于军队术语，2001 年后被广泛使用。

items.en: Latin roots are solid: latus, lateralis, com- are all well attested.
items.cn: 拉丁词根来源可靠：latus、lateralis、com- 均有充分文献。

note.en: Look-alikes share the lateralis root; near meanings sit around loan security.
note.cn: 形近共享 lateralis 词根；近义围绕贷款担保展开。

entries.definition: Of or relating to the side; collateral carries the same root with col- added.
entries.definitionCN: 侧面的；collateral 是这个词根加上 col-。

entries.definition: Between two sides or countries; same lateralis root.
entries.definitionCN: 双边的；同 lateralis 词根。

entries.definition: One-sided; same lateralis root.
entries.definitionCN: 单边的；同 lateralis 词根。

entries.definition: Having equal sides, as a triangle; same root.
A loan backed by collateral; collateral is what backs it.
entries.definitionCN: 以 collateral 作担保的贷款；collateral 是担保的东西。

entries.definition: A promise to repay; collateral is actual property pledged, not just a promise.
entries.definitionCN: 保证付款的承诺；collateral 是实际押出去的财产，不只是承诺。

entries.definition: Can mean a pledge, a financial asset, or safety; narrower than collateral in some uses.
entries.definitionCN: 可以指质押、金融资产或安全；某些用法比 collateral 更宽。

entries.definition: An initial lump sum; not security, but a partial commitment of value.
entries.definitionCN: 首付款；不是担保，而是价值的部分投入。

normalIntro.en: Real roots and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 真实词根与真实固定搭配。

normal.en: col- 'together' + lateralis 'of the side' = running alongside.
normal.cn: col-「一起」+ lateralis「侧面的」= 沿旁边走。

normal.en: latus 'side' is shared with lateral, bilateral, unilateral, equilateral.
normal.cn: latus「侧面」与 lateral、bilateral、unilateral、equilateral 同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: collateral damage, collateral evidence, put up collateral.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：collateral damage 附带损害、collateral evidence 旁证、put up collateral 提供抵押。

normal.en: The financial sense is property that sits alongside the loan.
normal.cn: 财务义就是坐在贷款旁边的财产。

normal.en: In medicine, collateral vessels run beside the main artery.
normal.cn: 医学里 collateral 血管沿主动脉旁边走。

abstract.en: Picture a row of houses beside a river with one house pledged to the bank.
abstract.cn: 想象河边一排房子，其中一栋被押给了银行。

abstract.en: Picture two parallel lines: one is the loan, the other is the collateral.
abstract.cn: 想象两条平行线：一条是贷款，一条是抵押品。

abstract.en: Picture a soldier aiming at a target while a bystander stands in the collateral line.
abstract.cn: 想象一个士兵瞄准目标，一个旁观者站在 collateral 线上。

examples.en: Small businesses struggled because banks demanded more collateral than they owned.
examples.cn: 小企业日子不好过，因为银行要求的抵押品比他们拥有的还多。

examples.en: The military said it did not expect significant collateral damage from the raid.
examples.cn: 军方表示预计这次突袭不会造成重大附带损害。

examples.en: Doctors opened a blocked artery with the help of collateral vessels that had grown around it.
examples.cn: 医生借助在堵塞动脉周围长出的侧支血管疏通了它。

dict_mnemonic.text: col-（一起）+ lateral（侧面）= 并排、附带 → 贷款旁边并排摆的东西 → 抵押品

root: 拉丁语 latus「侧面」→ lateralis「侧面的」→ 加前缀 col-（com- 的变体）→ collateralis「沿旁边走的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses extend from literal 'side by side' → accompanying/secondary → pledged property (financial borrowing of 'sitting beside') → side issue → medicine (side vessels) → bystander harm → supporting evidence → network backups.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从字面「并排」→ 伴随/次要 → 质押财产（财务上借「坐旁边」的想法）→ 次要问题 → 医学（侧支血管）→ 旁观者所受损害 → 旁证 → 网络备份。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two parallel lines, one the loan, one the property pledged beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条平行线，一条是贷款，一条是押在旁边的财产。

branches.en: THE LITERAL SIDE: running along the side of something.
branches.cn: 字面的「侧面」：沿着某物旁边走。

branches.en: SECONDARY THINGS: accompanying benefits or side issues.
branches.cn: 次要的事物：附带利益或次要问题。

branches.en: THE FINANCIAL USE: property that sits beside the loan.
branches.cn: 财务用法：坐在贷款旁边的财产。

branches.en: MEDICAL SIDE VESSELS: blood vessels running beside the main path.
branches.cn: 医学侧支血管：沿主通路旁边走的血管。

branches.en: WIDER FIGURATIVE USES: bystander harm, supporting evidence, network backups.
branches.cn: 更宽的比喻用法：旁观者受害、旁证、网络备份。

intro.en: Collateral builds on lateralis, itself from latus 'side', with col- as the 'together' prefix.
intro.cn: collateral 建立在 lateralis 之上，lateralis 来自 latus「侧面」，col- 是「一起」的前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin latus 'side' → lateralis → collateralis with col-.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 latus「侧面」→ lateralis → 加 col- 变成 collateralis。

items.meaning: of or pertaining to the side
items.exampleCN: collateralis 在 lateralis 前加 col-。

items.example: col- is a sound-changed form of com-.
items.exampleCN: col- 是 com- 在 l 前的音变形式。

items.example: The word travels from side-by-side to pledge.
items.exampleCN: 这个词从「并排」走到了「抵押品」。

items.example: Lateral movement is movement to the side.
items.exampleCN: lateral movement 就是向侧面运动。

items.example: A bilateral treaty sits between two states.
items.exampleCN: bilateral treaty 是两国之间的条约。

items.example: A unilateral decision is made by one side.
items.exampleCN: unilateral decision 是一方作出的决定。

items.example: An equilateral triangle has three equal sides.
items.exampleCN: 等边三角形有三条等长的边。

items.example: Lateralis uses -al as the adjective suffix.
items.exampleCN: Lateralis 用 -al 作形容词后缀。

items.example: The brain is lateralized for some functions.
items.exampleCN: 大脑某些功能是偏侧化的。

definition_zh: 租约；租期；出租；承租
definition_en: a legal contract by which someone rents property; the period of such a contract; to rent something out or to take it on rent
core_image: 一沓写满条款的合同，钥匙放在最后一页上
scene: 搬进公寓之前，两个人坐在桌前逐条看合同，最后在末尾签下名字。 They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
sceneCN: 这里是「租约」（第 1 个义项：租赁合同）；句意是他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。图中可辨识物件：合同、签字笔、钥匙。

derivatives.zh: 由 lease 与 hold 复合而成，义为「租赁权；租赁地产」
由 leasehold 加 -er 构成，义为「承租人；租赁权持有人」
由 lease 加 -ing 构成，义为「租赁；租赁业务」

senses.title: A legal contract for renting property
senses.definition: a legal agreement under which one party rents property from another for a period
senses.definitionCN: 一方在某一期限内向另一方租用财产的法定协议
senses.example: They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。
senses.why: The French source named a letting of property, so the contract is the central sense from which the others grow.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源指财产的出租，所以契约是中心义项，其他义项都由它长出。

senses.title: The period covered by a contract
senses.definition: the length of time for which such a contract runs
senses.definitionCN: 这种合同持续的时长
senses.example: The lease runs for three years and can be renewed.
senses.exampleCN: 租期三年，可以续签。
senses.why: A contract always fixes a stretch of time, so the document's name easily transfers to the years it covers.
senses.whyCN: 合同总会确定一段时间，所以文书的名字很容易转指它所覆盖的那些年。

senses.title: To rent property out to someone
senses.definition: to let someone use property in return for rent
senses.definitionCN: 收取租金，让别人使用自己的财产
senses.example: The family leases the upper floors to a small company.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人把楼上几层出租给一家小公司。
senses.why: If a contract lets someone use property, the owner can be said to lease it out, so the noun's name becomes a verb of granting.
senses.whyCN: 既然合同允许他人使用财产，所有者就可以说把财产出租出去，名词的名字于是变成表示授予的动词。

senses.title: To take and use property under a lease
senses.definition: to take property on a lease and pay rent for it
senses.definitionCN: 按租约取得财产使用权并支付租金
senses.example: We leased a car for the summer instead of buying one.
senses.exampleCN: 我们夏天租了一辆车，而不是买一辆。
senses.why: The same verb works from the other side of the contract: the tenant leases the thing that the landlord leases out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词也能从合同的另一边使用：租客承租的东西，正是房东出租的东西。

intro.en: Lease goes back to a Latin verb meaning to loosen or let go; through French it became the legal word for letting property to another person.
intro.cn: lease 可追溯到拉丁语中表示「放松、放开」的动词；经法语变成把财产让与他人使用的法律词。

items.en: The Latin adjective laxus meant loose or slack, not tightly held.
items.cn: 拉丁语形容词 laxus 意为松的、不紧的。

items.en: The verb laxare meant to loosen, release or let go.
items.cn: 动词 laxare 意为放松、放开或让出。

items.en: Old French lais named a letting of property, and laissier meant to let or leave.
items.cn: 古法语 lais 指财产的出租，动词 laissier 意为让出、留下。

items.en: Middle English les or lease named the contract and the right to hold land for a term.
items.cn: 中古英语 les 或 lease 指契约，以及按期限持有土地的权利。

items.en: Modern English keeps lease as both the contract and the act of renting out or taking on rent.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 lease 作名词指契约，也作动词指出租或承租。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the legal family and one same-root relative; the near-meaning group collects words for renting.
note.cn: 形近组收法律词族和一个同根词；近义组收表示租赁的词。

entries.definition: The right to hold property under a lease for a fixed term.
entries.definitionCN: 按租约在固定期限内持有财产的权利。

entries.definition: A person who holds property under a lease.
entries.definitionCN: 按租约持有财产的承租人。

entries.definition: To set free or let go; it shares the Latin verb laxare behind lease.
entries.definitionCN: 释放、放开；与 lease 共用背后的拉丁语动词 laxare。

entries.definition: A strap for holding an animal; only the spelling is close, with a different origin.
entries.definitionCN: 牵住动物的皮带；只是拼写相近，来源不同。

entries.definition: Money paid regularly for the use of property, or to pay it.
entries.definitionCN: 为使用财产定期支付的费用，或支付这笔费用。

entries.definition: To pay to use something for a short time.
entries.definitionCN: 付钱在短时间内使用某物。

entries.definition: To rent a house or room out to someone, chiefly in British English.
entries.definitionCN: 把房屋或房间出租给他人，主要用于英式英语。

entries.definition: To hire a ship or aircraft for a special purpose.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定用途租用船只或飞机。

normalIntro.en: A Latin verb of loosening becomes a legal noun; the family then adds holders and a near relative, release.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示「松开」的拉丁语动词变成法律名词；词族又添上持有人，以及近亲 release。

normal.en: Lease goes back to Latin laxare, to loosen, and the legal sense grows from letting property out of one's own hold.
normal.cn: lease 可追溯到拉丁语 laxare「松开」，法律义从「把财产从自己手里放出去」生长而来。

normal.en: The contract and the period share one word because a lease always fixes how long the arrangement lasts.
normal.cn: 契约与期限共用一个词，因为租约总要确定安排持续多久。

normal.en: Lease out is the landlord's direction, while lease from is the tenant's; the same verb serves both sides.
normal.cn: lease out 是房东的方向，lease from 是租客的方向；同一个动词服务双方。

normal.en: Leasehold and leaseholder add hold and -er to show the right and the person who holds it.
normal.cn: leasehold 与 leaseholder 加上 hold 和 -er，表明权利和持有权利的人。

normal.en: A new lease of life is a figurative lease: life is handed back for another term.
normal.cn: a new lease of life 是比喻性的租约：生命被重新交还一段时间。

abstract.en: To lease is to trade ownership for time, which is why the word sits between property and clock.
abstract.cn: 出租是用所有权换时间，所以这个词夹在财产与时钟之间。

abstract.en: A lease turns trust into paper: the arrangement survives even when the people who made it forget it.
abstract.cn: 租约把信任变成纸面：即使立约的人忘了，安排仍然存在。

abstract.en: The idea of loosening stays inside lease: something is let go for a while, then expected back.
abstract.cn: 「松开」的意思仍留在 lease 里：某物被放开一段时间，然后预期被归还。

examples.en: They signed a lease for the flat before the end of the month.
examples.cn: 他们在月底之前为公寓签了租约。

examples.en: The lease runs for three years and can be renewed.
examples.cn: 租期三年，可以续签。

examples.en: We leased a car for the summer instead of buying one.
examples.cn: 我们夏天租了一辆车，而不是买一辆。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「哩事」——租房合同里写满了「哩事」；lease 是租约。

root: 拉丁语 laxare（放松、放开）经古法语 lais（出租）进入中古英语 les/lease；与 lax、release 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a contract that lets property be used for a term; the senses divide into the period, the landlord's act and the tenant's act.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是允许他人在一定期限内使用财产的契约；义项由此分为租期、房东的出租和租客的承租。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of contract pages with a key resting on the last one.
core.cn: 核心意象：一沓合同纸，钥匙放在最后一页上。

branches.en: two people signing at the foot of a long document
branches.cn: 两人在一份长文件末尾签字

branches.en: a calendar with three years marked off
branches.cn: 标出三年时间的日历

branches.en: a landlord handing over a set of keys
branches.cn: 房东交出一串钥匙

branches.en: a family driving a rented car for one season
branches.cn: 一家人租一辆车用一个季节

branches.en: keys passed across a table after the ink dries
branches.cn: 墨迹干了以后钥匙在桌上递过去

intro.en: A Latin verb of loosening supplies the core, and English compounds with hold and suffixes for person and activity extend it.
intro.cn: 一个表示「松开」的拉丁语动词提供核心，英语再用 hold 构成复合词，并用表示人物和活动的后缀扩展。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

definition_zh: 房东；地主；（旧）旅店老板；客栈掌柜
definition_en: the person who owns a house or room and lets it to tenants, also a dated word for an innkeeper or the owner of land
core_image: 一个人站在自家楼门口，手里捏着一串钥匙和一沓房租收据
scene: 冬天的清晨，楼道里的暖气还没热起来。 The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
sceneCN: 这里 landlord 指「房东」（第 1 个义项）；句意为房东敲门来收房租。图中可辨识物件：楼门、钥匙串、房租收据。

derivatives.zh: 由 land 与 lady 复合，指女房东、女店主
由 landlord 加 -ism 构成，指地主收租的制度
由 landlord 加 -ing 构成，指出租房屋收租的行当

senses.title: The owner of property that is rented out
senses.definition: the person who owns a house, flat or room and lets it to someone who pays rent
senses.definitionCN: 拥有房屋、公寓或房间并出租给交租金者的人
senses.example: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 房东敲门来收房租。
senses.why: Once houses were let for money, the man who held the land also held the keys, so the compound shifted from owning ground to receiving rent.
senses.whyCN: 当房屋开始出租换钱，握有土地的人也握有钥匙，于是这个复合词从「拥有土地」转向「收取租金」。

senses.title: The keeper of an inn or a pub
senses.definition: a dated word for the man who runs an inn, a boarding house or a pub
senses.definitionCN: 较早的用法，指经营旅店、寄宿舍或酒馆的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
senses.exampleCN: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。
senses.why: An innkeeper owned the building he worked in, so the word for a property owner naturally covered the man behind the bar.
senses.whyCN: 旅店老板拥有自己经营的房子，因此「房产所有者」这个词自然也能指吧台后面的那个人。

senses.title: The lord of a manor
senses.definition: a historical word for the man who held land from a superior and ruled the tenants on it
senses.definitionCN: 历史用法，指从上级领有土地并管束其佃户的男子
senses.example: The landlord of the manor also judged disputes among his tenants.
senses.exampleCN: 庄园领主还裁决佃户之间的纠纷。
senses.why: In the feudal order land carried power, so landlord named not just an owner but the man whose word settled what happened on his ground.
senses.whyCN: 在封建秩序里土地意味着权力，因此 landlord 不只指所有者，还指那个一句话就能决定自己地界上事务的人。

intro.en: Landlord is a Middle English compound of land and lord, and lord itself goes back to an Old English word for the keeper of the loaf.
intro.cn: landlord 是中古英语由 land 与 lord 构成的复合词，而 lord 又可追到古英语中「掌管面包者」一词。

items.en: Land meant ground, territory or a country, and it is one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
items.cn: land 指土地、领土或国家，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

items.en: Hlaford, the ancestor of lord, first meant the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed those who depended on him.
items.cn: lord 的前身 hlaford 最初意为「掌管面包的人」，即供养依附者的男子。

items.en: Middle English joined land and lord into one compound for the man who owned or held land.
items.cn: 中古英语把 land 与 lord 合为一个复合词，指拥有或持有土地的人。

items.en: As more houses were let for rent, landlord widened from the owner of land to the owner of any rented property.
items.cn: 随着越来越多房屋出租，landlord 从土地所有者扩大到任何出租房产的所有者。

items.en: Modern English uses landlord for the person you pay rent to, and keeps the innkeeper sense in older or British pub use.
items.cn: 现代英语用 landlord 指收房租的人，旅店老板义则留在较早用法与英式酒馆说法里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects forms built on land or lord; the near-meaning group collects other words for people who own or manage property.
note.cn: 形近组收由 land 或 lord 构成的词；近义组收其他表示房产所有者或经营者的词。

entries.definition: A woman who owns property and lets it, or runs an inn.
The system in which landlords take rent from tenants.
entries.definitionCN: 地主向佃户收租的制度。

entries.definition: A master or nobleman, the second half of this compound.
entries.definitionCN: 主人或贵族，是这个词的后一半。

entries.definition: A person who legally possesses something.
The owner of a business or of property.
A person who grants a lease of property.
entries.definitionCN: 出租房产并授予租约的人。

entries.definition: A person who runs an inn.

normalIntro.en: The compound joins the oldest word for ground to the old word for a master, and its history moves from holding soil to collecting rent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词把最古老的「土地」一词与古老的「主人」一词结合，其历史从持有土地走向收取租金。

normal.en: Land is the ground itself, one of the oldest Germanic words in English.
normal.cn: land 就是土地本身，是英语中最古老的日耳曼词之一。

normal.en: Lord began as hlaford, the keeper of the loaf, the man who fed his household.
normal.cn: lord 起初是 hlaford，即掌管面包、供养一家人的人。

normal.en: Landlord is literally the lord of the land, the man whose word ruled his ground.
normal.cn: landlord 字面就是「土地之主」，他的话在自己地界上说了算。

normal.en: When renting spread, the lord of the land became the man who collects rent, while keeping his keys.
normal.cn: 当租房普及，土地之主变成了收房租的人，钥匙也仍在他手里。

normal.en: Landlady adds the female counterpart, and landlordism names the system rather than a person.
normal.cn: landlady 提供女性对应形式，landlordism 指制度而非某个人。

abstract.en: A compound can carry a whole social order: land plus master equals power over the people who live on it.
abstract.cn: 一个复合词能装下整套社会秩序：土地加主人，等于对住在上面的人的支配权。

abstract.en: The word did not change owners; it changed what owning meant, from soil to rent.
abstract.cn: 这个词换的不是所有者，而是「拥有」的含义：从泥土变为租金。

abstract.en: Keys and rent receipts are the modern costume of an old feudal title.
abstract.cn: 钥匙与房租收据，是一个古老封建头衔的现代装扮。

examples.en: The landlord knocked on the door to collect the rent.
examples.cn: 房东敲门来收房租。

examples.en: She has not paid the landlord this month.
examples.cn: 她这个月还没把房租交给房东。

examples.en: The landlord of the old inn kept a fire burning all winter.
examples.cn: 那家老旅店的老板整个冬天都让炉火不灭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「懒得劳动」——懒得劳动的地主靠收租过日子；谐音记住 landlord 是房东、地主。

root: 由古英语 land（土地）与 lord（前身 hlaford，掌管面包者）复合而成；指拥有土地或出租房产的人。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the man who holds land and lets others use it; from there it names the rent collector, the innkeeper and the feudal lord.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是持有土地并让别人使用的人；由此分出收房租者、旅店老板与封建领主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a man at a doorway holding keys and a bundle of rent receipts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人站在门口，手里拿着钥匙和一沓房租收据。

branches.en: a knock at the door on rent day
branches.cn: 收租日的一次敲门

branches.en: a tenant handing over an envelope of cash
branches.cn: 房客递上一个装现金的信封

branches.en: a manor court settling a dispute
branches.cn: 庄园法庭裁决一场纠纷

branches.en: a fire kept burning in an old inn
branches.cn: 老旅店里整夜不灭的炉火

branches.en: a pub keeper wiping the counter
branches.cn: 酒馆掌柜擦着柜台

intro.en: The word is a Germanic compound of two Old English nouns, and English suffixes later build abstract and feminine forms from it.
intro.cn: 这个词是两个古英语名词组成的日耳曼复合词，后来英语后缀又由它造出抽象名词与女性形式。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this compound; both of its parts are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，它的两个组成部分都属日耳曼语。

definition_zh: 实习；实习期；实习岗位
definition_en: a period of work in a company or organization, often for a student, in order to gain experience
core_image: 一张写着名字的工作牌，压在办公桌一角，旁边是还没拆封的笔记本
scene: 毕业生把新办的门禁卡挂在胸前，在办公室的空位上坐下开始整理资料。 Her summer internship turned into a full job offer.
sceneCN: 这里 internship 是「实习」（第 1 个义项：为获取经验的短期工作），句意为她的暑期实习最后变成了正式录用。画面里的物件：门禁卡、办公桌、资料夹。

pos.zh: 名词：实习；实习期；实习岗位

derivatives.zh: 去后缀 -ship 构成，义为「实习生」
由 intern 加 -ing 构成，义为「实习的过程」
同一后缀构成，义为「学徒期」

senses.title: A first taste of work
senses.definition: a job taken mainly to learn, usually for a fixed period and often by a student
senses.definitionCN: 主要为学习而承担的工作，通常有固定期限，多为学生去做
senses.example: His first real internship was in a hospital kitchen.
senses.exampleCN: 他的第一份正经实习是在医院的厨房里。
senses.why: The suffix -ship means a state or role, so an internship is the condition of being an intern.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 表示状态或身份，所以 internship 就是「做 intern 的那段时光」。

senses.title: The period itself
senses.definition: the length of time during which someone works as an intern
senses.definitionCN: 某人做实习生所经历的那段时间
senses.example: The internship lasts twelve weeks with a review at the end.
senses.exampleCN: 这期实习持续十二周，结束时有一次评估。
senses.why: Time became as concrete as the job: the word names both the post and its run.
senses.whyCN: 时间变得和岗位一样具体：这个词同时指岗位和它的期限。

senses.title: A training step in a profession
senses.definition: a required supervised stage before full professional practice
senses.definitionCN: 正式执业之前必须经历的带督导训练阶段
senses.example: Medical internships keep young doctors under close watch.
senses.exampleCN: 医学实习让年轻医生处在密切看护之下。
senses.why: Law and medicine took the word over for the stage that makes someone fully qualified.
senses.whyCN: 法律与医学借用了这个词，指让人取得正式资格的那一段。

intro.en: Internship is an English coinage: the Latin-derived internal plus the native noun suffix -ship.
intro.cn: internship 是英语自造的：拉丁来源的 intern 加上本土名词后缀 -ship。

items.en: Internus "inner" described what lies within.
items.cn: internus「内部的」描述位于里侧的东西。

items.en: French interne named a doctor living inside a hospital.
items.cn: 法语 interne 指住在医院里的医生。

items.en: American English used intern for a graduate in training.
items.cn: 美式英语用 intern 指正在受训的毕业生。

items.en: -scipe was the native suffix for state or rank.
items.cn: 古英语的 -scipe 是表示状态或身份的本土后缀。

items.en: The two were joined in the early twentieth century as internship.
items.cn: 两者在二十世纪初合成 internship。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the intern stem; the near-meaning group holds other words for learning on the job.
note.cn: 形近组共用 intern 词干；近义组收其他表示「在工作中学习」的词。

entries.definition: Inside a thing, a body, or a country.
The person doing such a period of work.
The state of being friends.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「友谊」，共用 -ship 后缀。

entries.definition: Training under a skilled master for years.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「学徒期」，跟师傅学多年。

entries.definition: A paid training post, often in Europe.
entries.definitionCN: 名词义为「带薪培训岗位」。

entries.definition: A trial period watched by an employer or court.

normalIntro.en: These hooks connect the word to your own first days at a desk.
normalIntro.cn: 这些钩子把它挂在你第一次坐进办公桌的那几天上。

normal.en: Intern plus -ship, the suffix of state, as in friendship.
normal.cn: intern 加 -ship，那个表示状态的后缀，如同 friendship。

normal.en: An intern is a person; an internship is the thing they go through.
normal.cn: intern 是人，internship 是他们经历的那件事。

normal.en: Summer internship is the phrase on every student's list.
normal.cn: summer internship 是每个学生清单上的词。

normal.en: The badge you wear is the sign of the internship.
normal.cn: 胸前那张工作牌就是实习的标志。

normal.en: -ship appears again in leadership and friendship.
normal.cn: -ship 还出现在 leadership 与 friendship 里。

abstract.en: An internship is a shadow before the real body arrives.
abstract.cn: 实习是真正上岗之前的一道影子。

abstract.en: It is a room you borrow so you can learn the trade.
abstract.cn: 那是你借用的房间，为的是学会这门手艺。

abstract.en: Practice, with a name tag.
abstract.cn: 练习，外加一张名牌。

examples.en: She found the internship through a friend of her mother.
examples.cn: 她通过母亲的一位朋友找到了这份实习。

examples.en: An internship at a newspaper taught him to write fast.
examples.cn: 在报社的实习教会他快速写稿。

examples.en: Unpaid internships became a topic of public debate.
examples.cn: 无薪实习成了公众讨论的话题。

dict_mnemonic.text: intern（实习生）+ ship（身份状态）——做实习生的那段身份

root: 拉丁语 internus「内部的」→ 法语 interne「驻院医生」→ 英语 intern，加本土后缀 -ship（状态、身份）成 internship。同族有 intern、internal、apprenticeship。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: the learning post, the period it lasts, and the required stage in a profession.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：学习性质的岗位、这段岗位持续的时间，以及专业执业前的必修阶段。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a borrowed desk where learning is the real salary.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张借来的桌子，真正的报酬是学到的本事。

branches.en: THE DESK: the first job taken to learn.
branches.cn: 书桌这条线：为学习而做的第一份工作。

branches.en: THE CALENDAR: the weeks the post lasts.
branches.cn: 日历这条线：这份岗位持续的周数。

branches.en: THE EXAM: the supervised stage before a licence.
branches.cn: 考试这条线：拿执照前的带督导阶段。

branches.en: THE LADDER: both senses sit on the way up to doing the job alone.
branches.cn: 阶梯线：两个义项都在通往独立执业的路上。

branches.en: THE CLOCK: training is measured out in fixed time.
branches.cn: 时钟线：训练总是按固定时长来计算。

intro.en: Internship pairs the Latin stem intern- "inside" with the Old English suffix -ship.
intro.cn: internship 把拉丁词干 intern-「在内」与古英语后缀 -ship 配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin internus and French interne are recorded; -ship is native Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 internus 与法语 interne 均有记载，而 -ship 是日耳曼语本土后缀。

items.example: It names someone living inside an institution.
items.exampleCN: 它指住在机构内部的人。

items.example: The noun is the base of the whole word.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整条词的基础。
这个词干来自这个形容词。

items.example: The French form fixed the practical sense.
items.exampleCN: 法语形式定下了实用义。

items.example: It shows how -ship attaches to a noun.
items.exampleCN: 它示范了 -ship 如何接在名词后。

items.example: An apprenticeship is the older cousin.
items.exampleCN: apprenticeship 是它更年长的表亲。

items.example: The suffix works the same way here.
items.exampleCN: 后缀在这里起同样作用。

definition_zh: 负有责任的；须作交代的；可解释的
definition_en: required to explain one's actions, or able to be explained
core_image: 会议室里，负责人把每个决定逐条摊开说明
scene: 项目失败后，负责人被要求公开说明每一个决定。 Managers are accountable for the decisions they make.
sceneCN: 这里的 accountable 指「负有责任的」（第 1 个义项：必须为自己的行为作出交代）；句意是管理者要为自己作出的决定负责。

pos.zh: 负有责任的；须作交代的；可解释的

senses.title: Required to answer
senses.definition: required to explain one's decisions to someone with authority to judge them
senses.definitionCN: 必须向有权评判的一方解释自己的决定
senses.example: Managers are accountable for the decisions they make.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者要为自己作出的决定负责。
senses.why: A person who must give an account of money held was once literally made to count it out, and the adjective kept that image of answering.
senses.whyCN: 必须交代经手钱款的人，当年真的要一笔笔数出来，这个形容词保留了那幅「当众作答」的画面。

senses.title: Able to be explained
senses.definition: capable of being explained or justified
senses.definitionCN: 能够被说明或证明其合理
senses.example: There is no accountable reason for the delay.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误没有说得通的理由。
senses.why: If an act can be accounted for, it can be given a reason, and this older, quieter sense uses account in the sense of explanation.
senses.whyCN: 一件事若能 account for，就能给出理由；这个较旧、较安静的意思用的正是 account 的「说明」义。

intro.en: The adjective is the old noun for a reckoning with an ending meaning required to.
intro.cn: 这个形容词是表示「算账」的旧名词加上「应负……」的词尾。

items.en: computare meant to count up or settle.
items.cn: computare 意为结算、清点。

items.en: aconter meant to render an account.
items.cn: aconter 意为作出交代。

items.en: account named the reckoning of money entrusted.
items.cn: account 指对所托钱款的结算。

items.en: accountable described stewards who must answer for what they held.
items.cn: accountable 描述必须为所管财物作答的管事。

items.en: the word spread to officials, companies and parents alike.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到官员、公司与家长身上。

note.en: The look-alike group is the account family; the near-meaning group names responsibility and explainability.
note.cn: 形近组是 account 词族；近义组表示责任与可解释性。

entries.definition: the duty to explain one's actions
a person who keeps financial records
a record or explanation
having a duty to deal with something
legally answerable for something
required to explain to an authority
able to be explained
open about actions and money

normalIntro.en: These hints follow the old picture of a steward counting out what he held.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条贴着旧日管事把经手财物一笔笔数出来的画面。

normal.en: accountable means a person from whom an account can be demanded.
normal.cn: accountable 意为可以被要求交出账目的人。

normal.en: the -able ending here is not able to but required to.
normal.cn: 这里的 -able 不是「能够」，而是「应当」。

normal.en: managers are accountable to those above and to those they serve.
normal.cn: 管理者对上也对下负责。

normal.en: holding someone accountable is asking for the reckoning in public.
normal.cn: 追究责任，就是公开要那份账。

normal.en: an accountable reason is one that can be counted out and found sound.
normal.cn: 说得通的理由，是能一条条摆出来还站得住的理由。

abstract.en: Picture a steward laying coins on a table before his lord.
abstract.cn: 想象管事把一枚枚钱币摆到主人面前。

abstract.en: See a manager standing beside a chart, explaining each step.
abstract.cn: 想象负责人站在图表旁，逐条解释。

abstract.en: Think of a door marked with a name and a duty.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门上写着姓名与职责。

examples.en: Managers are accountable for the decisions they make.
examples.cn: 管理者要为自己作出的决定负责。

examples.en: There is no accountable reason for the delay.
examples.cn: 这次延误没有说得通的理由。

examples.en: The minister is accountable to parliament.
examples.cn: 这位部长向议会负责。

dict_mnemonic.text: account（交代账目）+ -able（应……的）——应当把账交代出来的，就是「负有责任的」。

root: 由 account 加 -able 构成，account 源自拉丁语 computare（计算），本义「应当交代账目的」，引申为负有责任、可解释。

sensesIntro.en: One adjective covers the official who must answer and the excuse that can be answered for.
sensesIntro.cn: 同一个形容词，既管必须作答的官员，也管经得起追问的理由。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a steward counting coins before his lord.
core.cn: 核心意象：管事在主人面前清点钱币。

branches.en: a manager explaining a failed project
branches.cn: 为失败项目作解释的负责人

branches.en: a minister standing before parliament
branches.cn: 站在议会面前的部长

branches.en: a delay that has a reason behind it
branches.cn: 背后找得到原因的延误

branches.en: a decision that can be justified step by step
branches.cn: 能一步步证明合理的决定

branches.en: to be answerable and to be answerable for are the same root
branches.cn: 「须作答」与「可作答」本是同一个词根

intro.en: The word is a root for counting with an ending that marks obligation.
intro.cn: 这个词是表示「计算」的词根加一个表示义务的词尾。

latinIntro.en: The root putare, to reckon, also gives compute and dispute.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 putare（计算）还给出 compute 与 dispute。

definition_zh: 悬崖；峭壁；急剧下跌
definition_en: a high steep face of rock, especially at the edge of the sea, or a sudden sharp fall in an amount
core_image: 海浪拍打的那面笔直石壁
scene: 海风很大，脚下的岩石忽然断成一面陡壁。 A narrow path runs along the cliff above the bay.
sceneCN: 这里 cliff 指「悬崖」（第 1 个义项：高而陡的岩壁）；句意是海湾上方有一条窄路沿着悬崖延伸。

pos.zh: 悬崖；峭壁；（数额的）急剧下跌

senses.title: A steep rock face
senses.definition: a high steep surface of rock, often beside the sea
senses.definitionCN: 常常位于海边的又高又陡的岩壁
senses.example: Waves broke against the foot of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 海浪拍打着悬崖脚下。
senses.why: The old word named a steep rock, and the sea coast is where such rock is most often seen.
senses.whyCN: 这个古老的词本指陡峭的岩石，而海岸正是这种岩石最常见的地方。

senses.title: The edge of a dangerous drop
senses.definition: a position of sudden danger where a small step can be fatal
senses.definitionCN: 一步之差就可能致命的危险处境
senses.example: The company stood on the cliff edge of bankruptcy.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司站在破产的危险边缘。
senses.why: Standing at the top of a cliff gives a clear picture of danger close at hand.
senses.whyCN: 站在崖顶能形象地表现危险近在咫尺。

senses.title: A sharp fall in a level
senses.definition: a sudden large drop in prices, sales or numbers
senses.definitionCN: 价格、销量或数字的突然大幅下降
senses.example: Sales went over the cliff after the recall.
senses.exampleCN: 召回事件之后销量一落千丈。
senses.why: A graph that drops almost straight down looks like a cliff, so the word moved into business talk.
senses.whyCN: 图表上几乎垂直落下的曲线像悬崖，这个词便进入了商业用语。

intro.en: Cliff is an old English word for steep rock; it was never borrowed from Latin.
intro.cn: cliff 是表示陡峭岩石的古英语词，并非借自拉丁语。

items.en: Clif meant a steep rock or a high shore.
items.cn: clif 指陡峭的岩石或高高的海岸。

items.en: Related forms in German and Dutch also named steep rock.
items.cn: 德语和荷兰语中的相关形式同样指陡峭的岩石。

items.en: The spelling settled as cliff and the sea sense grew strong.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 cliff，与海相关的含义变得突出。

items.en: Cliff top and cliff face became common everyday compounds.
items.cn: cliff top 与 cliff face 成为常见的日常复合词。

items.en: The noun now also describes a sudden fall in figures.
items.cn: 这个名词如今也用来形容数字的突然下跌。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short words that resemble cliff in spelling, while the meaning group names kinds of steep rock or high land.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写接近 cliff 的短词，近义组列出各类陡岩与高地。

entries.definition: to cut something with scissors or to fasten it
entries.definitionCN: 用剪刀剪，或把东西夹住

entries.definition: a deep narrow opening in rock or in the ground
entries.definitionCN: 岩石或地面上的深窄裂口

entries.definition: an old poetic word for a region with a certain climate
entries.definitionCN: 古诗文中指某种气候的地区

entries.definition: a very steep side of a high rock or mountain
entries.definitionCN: 高岩或高山的极陡侧壁

entries.definition: a high steep bank beside a river or the sea
entries.definitionCN: 河岸或海岸边高而陡的坡

entries.definition: a high rough mass of rock on a hill

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the straight rock wall, the sea below and the graph that falls like a stone.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从笔直岩壁、崖下海水和笔直下坠的曲线入手。

normal.en: Cliff is one short syllable, as abrupt as the drop it names.
normal.cn: cliff 只有一个短音节，就像它所指的落差那样突然。

normal.en: Change one letter in clip and you get cliff: a clip cuts, a cliff cuts the land short.
normal.cn: 把 clip 改一个字母就是 cliff：剪刀剪开东西，悬崖把陆地截断。

normal.en: Sea cliffs are the most common picture, so the coast is the natural scene.
normal.cn: 海崖是最常见的画面，所以海岸是它最自然的场景。

normal.en: A cliffhanger leaves you hanging at the edge of the story.
normal.cn: cliffhanger 就是把你吊在故事边缘的悬念。

normal.en: A sales graph that drops straight down is called a cliff in business talk.
normal.cn: 在商业说法里，直线下坠的销量图就叫悬崖。

abstract.en: Picture a white wall of rock with seabirds circling the top.
abstract.cn: 想象一面白色的岩壁，海鸟在崖顶盘旋。

abstract.en: Picture a narrow footpath with nothing but air on the left.
abstract.cn: 想象一条窄窄的小路，左侧空无一物。

abstract.en: Picture a line on a chart that falls almost straight down.
abstract.cn: 想象图表上一条几乎是垂直落下的线。

examples.en: They watched the sun set from the top of the cliff.
examples.cn: 他们从崖顶看日落。

examples.en: The path along the cliff is closed after heavy rain.
examples.cn: 大雨之后，沿着悬崖的那条小路封闭了。

examples.en: Profits fell off a cliff in the second quarter.
examples.cn: 第二季度利润断崖式下跌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 cliff 想成被刀削过的一刀：陆地到此忽然被切断，剩下一面直壁。

root: 源自古英语 clif（陡峭的岩石、高海岸），属日耳曼语族，本义就是直立的岩壁。

sensesIntro.en: From a wall of coastal rock to the danger of standing at its edge, then to a graph that drops like a stone.
sensesIntro.cn: 从海边岩壁，到站在崖边的危险，再到像石头般下坠的曲线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a straight wall of rock with the sea at its foot.
core.cn: 核心意象：一面笔直的岩壁，脚下就是海水。

branches.en: The basic sense is the rock wall itself, usually beside water.
branches.cn: 基本义就是那面岩壁，通常临水而立。

branches.en: Standing at the top turns the rock into a picture of danger.
branches.cn: 站在崖顶使这块岩石成为危险的写照。

branches.en: A line that plunges on a chart borrows the shape of the rock.
branches.cn: 图表上暴跌的曲线借用了岩壁的形状。

branches.en: The physical edge and the risky position share one image.
branches.cn: 物理的边缘与危险的处境共用一个意象。

branches.en: Both senses rest on the idea of a sudden vertical line.
branches.cn: 两个义项都建立在突然垂直落下这一形象上。

intro.en: The word takes no prefix, so its family is built from compounds and a few endings.
intro.cn: 这个词不加前缀，家族由复合词和少量词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin base here; the root is the Old English noun for steep rock.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词基，词根是古英语中表示陡岩的名词。

items.meaning: more than one steep rock face
items.example: The cliffs run for ten miles along the coast.
items.exampleCN: 这些悬崖沿海岸延伸十里。

items.meaning: full of cliffs or steep rock
items.example: The island is wild and cliffy.

items.meaning: the land at the side of a cliff
items.example: A small house stands on the cliffside.
The wall rose in clifflike layers.
items.exampleCN: 那堵墙像悬崖一样层层高起。

items.meaning: the flat ground at the top of a cliff
items.example: We had lunch on the clifftop.

items.meaning: an ending that leaves the audience in suspense
items.example: The series ended on a cliffhanger.

items.meaning: the vertical surface of a cliff
items.example: Climbers study the cliff face first.

items.meaning: the very border where the rock falls away
items.example: Keep back from the cliff edge.

definition_zh: 虫；蠕虫；蚯蚓；蠕动着前进；逐步套取（消息）
definition_en: a small soft creature with a long thin body and no legs, or to move slowly by twisting like one
core_image: 一块翻开的湿土里，一条细长的身体一缩一伸地往前移
scene: 雨后的小路上，几条蚯蚓被水冲出来，在石头上慢慢扭。 The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
sceneCN: 这里 worm 是「虫、蠕虫」（第 1 个义项：身体细长柔软、没有腿的小生物）；句意为那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没了影。湿土里一缩一伸的细长身体，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worm 加 -y 构成，义为「多虫的；虫蛀的」
由 worm 加 -like 构成，义为「像虫的；细长的」
由 silk 与 worm 复合，义为「蚕」

senses.title: The legless creature
senses.definition: a small soft animal with a long thin body and no legs, living in soil or water
senses.definitionCN: 身体细长柔软、没有腿的小动物，生活在土里或水中
senses.example: After the rain the worms came up and lay on the path.
senses.exampleCN: 雨后虫子钻出土来，躺在小路上。
senses.why: This is the creature itself, the shape of which drives every other sense.
senses.whyCN: 这就是这种生物本身，它的形状驱动了其余所有义项。

senses.title: To move like one
senses.definition: to move slowly and with difficulty by twisting the body close to the ground
senses.definitionCN: 贴着地扭动身体，缓慢艰难地移动
senses.example: The dog wormed its way under the gate and was gone before anyone noticed.
senses.exampleCN: 那条狗从大门底下钻了过去，谁也没注意到它就没影了。
senses.why: The verb borrows the body's way of travelling: no legs, no hurry, just twisting forward.
senses.whyCN: 动词借用了这种身体的走法：没有腿，也不急，只是一路扭过去。

senses.title: To pull secrets out bit by bit
senses.definition: to get information out of someone slowly and indirectly, as in worm something out of someone
senses.definitionCN: 慢慢间接地从他人那里取得消息，如 worm something out of someone
senses.example: It took her an hour to worm the truth out of him.
senses.exampleCN: 她花了一个小时才从他嘴里套出实情。
senses.why: Wriggling into a narrow place is exactly how one gets into another person's confidence step by step.
senses.whyCN: 往窄缝里慢慢钻，正是人一步步钻进别人心事里的样子。

senses.title: The wretched person
senses.definition: a mean and contemptible person, used as a word of low abuse
senses.definitionCN: 卑劣可鄙的人，用作轻蔑的骂词
senses.example: Nobody trusted the worm who had sold the plans to a rival.
senses.exampleCN: 没人信任那个把图纸卖给对手的可鄙家伙。
senses.why: A creature that lives by creeping and twisting easily becomes a picture of a person who betrays.
senses.whyCN: 靠钻营扭动过活的生物，很容易变成背叛者的画像。

senses.title: The one who turns at last
senses.definition: used in the saying the worm turns, meaning even the most patient person will resist
senses.definitionCN: 用于谚语 the worm turns，意即最忍让的人也会反抗
senses.example: He said nothing for years, and then the worm turned.
senses.exampleCN: 他多年不作声，后来终于翻脸了。
senses.why: Even a body with no strength can turn, and that turning is the proverb's whole point.
senses.whyCN: 就连毫无力气的身体也能扭过来，这个「扭」就是整句谚语的要点。

intro.en: Worm is Old English wyrm, which first meant a serpent, and only later narrowed to the small creatures of soil.
intro.cn: worm 来自古英语 wyrm，最初指蛇，后来才收窄为土里的小虫。

items.en: wyrm meant a snake or a dragon, the long bending body, not the small soil creature.
items.cn: wyrm 指蛇或龙，是那细长扭动的身体，并非土中小虫。

items.en: The same word for serpent appears in Norse and German forms.
items.cn: 表示蛇的同一词出现在北欧与德语的形式中。

items.en: Latin vermis, a worm, lived beside it in learned writing and reinforced the small-creature sense.
items.cn: 拉丁语 vermis（虫）在学术写作中与之并存，强化了小虫之义。

items.en: The meaning narrowed to small soft creatures, while dragon survived only in old poetry.
items.cn: 词义收窄为柔软的小生物，龙义仅存于古诗。

items.en: The verb grew out of the creature's way of moving, and then out of its way of getting in.
items.cn: 动词先由它移动的方式长出来，再延伸到它钻进去的方式。

note.en: The first group holds the derived forms, the second holds other small creatures that people confuse it with.
note.cn: 第一组收派生形式，第二组收容易与它混淆的其他小生物。

entries.definition: More than one worm.
Full of worms, or eaten by them.
The caterpillar that spins silk.
A small creature with six legs and a body in three parts.
A long thin animal with no legs and scales.
The wormlike young of a butterfly or moth.

normalIntro.en: Worm is a short old word whose first meaning was snake, and whose shape still drives its metaphors.
normalIntro.cn: worm 是一个短小的古词，最初指蛇，它的形状至今驱动着各种比喻。

normal.en: Worm rhymes with term, and unlike warm it keeps a short crisp vowel.
normal.cn: worm 与 term 押韵，与 warm 不同，元音短而紧。

normal.en: The first meaning was snake, so a worm in old texts may be something larger.
normal.cn: 最初义是蛇，所以旧文本里的 worm 可能是个更大的东西。

normal.en: Silkworm and tapeworm show the word joining with another to name a kind.
normal.cn: silkworm 与 tapeworm 显示它与另一词结合来指某一类。

normal.en: Worm out of means pull out slowly, like a thread pulled by twisting.
normal.cn: worm out of 指慢悠悠地拽出来，像扭着拉一根线。

normal.en: The worm turns comes from the idea that even a soft body will finally wriggle free.
normal.cn: the worm turns 源自「再软的身体最后也会扭开」的想象。

abstract.en: A thin body folding and unfolding through wet soil.
abstract.cn: 细长的身体在湿土里一折一伸。

abstract.en: A shape with no eyes, no legs, and no pause.
abstract.cn: 一个没有眼睛、没有腿、也不停下的形状。

abstract.en: A body that moves by giving up its own straightness.
abstract.cn: 一个靠放弃笔直而前进的身体。

examples.en: The child put the worm back into the soil gently.
examples.cn: 孩子轻轻把蚯蚓放回土里。

examples.en: He wormed through the narrow gap behind the shelf.
examples.cn: 他从架子后面的窄缝里挤了过去。

examples.en: She wormed the whole story out of her brother at dinner.
examples.cn: 晚饭时她把整件事从弟弟嘴里套了出来。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我摸」——土里一摸，摸到一条软软的虫。

root: 古英语 wyrm（蛇；龙），与德语、北欧语同源；拉丁语 vermis（虫）在后世加强「小虫」义。

sensesIntro.en: The creature comes first, then its way of moving, then its way of creeping into secrets, then the abuse, and finally the revolt.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是这种生物，再是它移动的样子，接着是它钻进秘密的方式，然后是骂人语，最后是反抗。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin body folding through wet soil.
core.cn: 核心意象：湿土里一折一伸的细长身体。

branches.en: The creature branch: worms lying on the path after rain.
branches.cn: 生物分支：雨后躺在路上的虫。

branches.en: The movement branch: a dog wriggling under the gate.
branches.cn: 移动分支：从门下钻过的狗。

branches.en: The secret branch: pulling the truth out slowly.
branches.cn: 秘密分支：慢慢套出实情。

branches.en: The abuse branch: the one who sold the plans.
branches.cn: 骂词分支：卖图纸的那个人。

branches.en: The revolt branch: silence that finally breaks.
branches.cn: 反抗分支：终于打破的沉默。

intro.en: Worm is a bare stem; -y and -like build adjectives, and compounds name whole families of creatures.
intro.cn: worm 是裸词干；-y 与 -like 构成形容词，复合词则命名一整类生物。

latinIntro.en: The stem is Germanic, but Latin vermis lived beside it and left its own traces, such as vermin.
latinIntro.cn: 词干属日耳曼语，但拉丁语 vermis 与之并存，并留下了 vermin 之类的痕迹。

items.exampleCN: 它构成 vermin 与 vermicelli。

definition_zh: 无论何时；每当；随时；几时都行
definition_en: at any time at all, or every time that, used when the exact moment does not matter or keeps repeating
core_image: 一只钟没有指针，只有一圈刻度，随便指哪一格都行
scene: 店主把营业时间牌翻过来，只写一行：想来就来。 Whenever you pass by, the door is open.
sceneCN: 这里 whenever 是「无论何时」（第 1 个义项：任何时刻都可以）；句意为你什么时候路过，门都是开的。一只没有指针、只剩一圈刻度的钟就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: At any time
senses.definition: used to say that any moment is acceptable or possible
senses.definitionCN: 表示任何时刻都可以或都可能
senses.example: Whenever you pass by, the door is open.
senses.exampleCN: 你什么时候路过，门都是开的。
senses.why: The suffix -ever turns the time question into a total, so no particular hour is being asked for.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ever 把时间问句变成全称，于是并不索取某一个具体钟点。

senses.title: Every time that
senses.definition: used to say that something happens each time a certain event occurs
senses.definitionCN: 表示每当某一事件发生，某事就随之发生
senses.example: Whenever it rains, the road floods near the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 每逢下雨，桥边的路就积水。
senses.why: If every moment qualifies, then each repeated case qualifies too, so the blanket word covers habitual events.
senses.whyCN: 若每个时刻都算数，那么每一次重复的情形也算数，于是这个全称词能覆盖习惯性事件。

senses.title: Said alone, meaning any time suits
senses.definition: used as a short answer to say that no particular time is better
senses.definitionCN: 作简短回答，表示没有哪个时间更合适
senses.example: Whenever. I am free all week.
senses.exampleCN: 什么时候都行，我这一周都有空。
senses.why: One word can replace a whole list of acceptable hours, so the compound becomes a complete answer.
senses.whyCN: 一个词足以替代一整套可接受的时间，于是这个复合词本身成了完整回答。

intro.en: Whenever is the Middle English union of when and ever, the same pattern that produced whoever and wherever.
intro.cn: whenever 是中古英语里 when 与 ever 的结合，与 whoever、wherever 出自同一模式。

items.en: Hwænne and æfre stood as two separate words with no compound yet.
items.cn: hwænne 与 æfre 仍是两个分开的词，尚无复合形式。

items.en: Writers joined them into whenever, which took over the sense of at any time that.
items.cn: 作者把它们连成 whenever，由此接管了「在任何时候」的意思。

items.en: The word spread in instructions and promises, where the exact time is deliberately left open.
items.cn: 这个词在说明与承诺中传开，因为那里的具体时间被有意留空。

items.en: In speech it shortened into a single answer, often said with a shrug.
items.cn: 在口语里它缩短成一个单词的回答，常伴以耸肩。

items.en: Set phrases such as whenever possible and whenever necessary fixed it in formal prose.
items.cn: whenever possible、whenever necessary 等固定短语把它钉在正式文字中。

note.en: The first group gathers the -ever family, the second the words for repeated or open timing.
note.cn: 第一组收 -ever 词族，第二组收表示反复或开放时间的说法。

entries.definition: The plain question word without the total sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不带全称意味的普通疑问词

entries.definition: The place version of the same compound.
The person version of the same compound.
The thing version of the same compound.
The repeating sense of whenever in ordinary words.
The open sense of whenever written as a phrase.
Always, the strictest version of the open sense.

normalIntro.en: It is when plus ever, so the question loses its point and becomes a wide open schedule.
normalIntro.cn: 它是 when 加 ever，于是问句失去了尖，变成一张广开的日程表。

normal.en: The -ever suffix makes any wh word total: whenever, wherever, whoever.
normal.cn: -ever 词尾把每个 wh 词变成全称：whenever、wherever、whoever。

normal.en: Whenever possible is the most common pairing, and it leaves the hour blank.
normal.cn: whenever possible 是最常见的搭配，它把钟点留空。

normal.en: Every time is the plain English of whenever in its habitual sense.
normal.cn: every time 就是 whenever 在习惯义上的白话说法。

normal.en: Said alone, it is a shrug with a timetable on it.
normal.cn: 单独说出来，它是一张写着时间表的耸肩。

normal.en: Ask when, answer whenever: the question has dissolved.
normal.cn: 问 when，答 whenever：问题自己消解了。

abstract.en: See a clock with no hands.
abstract.cn: 看一只没有指针的钟。

abstract.en: Feel an open door in any weather.
abstract.cn: 感觉任何天气里都敞着的门。

abstract.en: Hear rain arrive and the road flood again.
abstract.cn: 听雨来，桥边的路又积水。

examples.en: Come whenever you have a little time.
examples.cn: 你什么时候有点时间就来。

examples.en: Whenever I cook rice, I make too much.
examples.cn: 我每次煮米饭都会煮多。

examples.en: Whenever possible. We take the early train.
examples.cn: 只要有可能，我们就坐早班车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温艾佛」——温先生和艾佛说：什么时候来都行。

root: 中古英语 when + ever 复合；同族有 whichever、wherever、whoever。

sensesIntro.en: The word covers any hour, then stretches over every repeated occasion, and finally stands alone as a complete answer.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先包揽任何一个钟点，再延伸到每一次重复的情形，最后单独站成一个完整的回答。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a clock with no hands on the wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙上挂着一只没有指针的钟。

branches.en: The open branch: the door is open whenever you pass.
branches.cn: 开放分支：你什么时候路过门都开着。

branches.en: The habitual branch: whenever it rains, the road floods.
branches.cn: 习惯分支：每逢下雨路就积水。

branches.en: The answer branch: whenever, I am free all week.
branches.cn: 回答分支：随时都行，我一周都有空。

branches.en: The formal branch: whenever possible in written rules.
branches.cn: 正式分支：书面规定里的 whenever possible。

branches.en: The family branch: wherever and whoever built the same way.

definition_zh: 赤裸的；光秃的；勉强的；露出
definition_en: not covered by clothes or anything else, or only just enough
core_image: 冬天的树枝光秃秃地伸向天空
scene: 雪化了，院子里一片安静。 The trees stood bare against the sky.
sceneCN: 这里 bare 是「光秃的」（第 2 个义项：没有叶子或覆盖物）；句意是树木光秃秃地立在天空下。

pos.zh: 形容词：赤裸的；光秃的；勉强的

derivatives.zh: 由 bare 加 -ly 构成，义为「几乎不；仅仅」
由 bare 加 -ness 构成，义为「赤裸；荒芜」
由 bare 加 -ing 构成，义为「露出」

senses.title: Not covered
senses.definition: not covered by clothes or a covering
senses.definitionCN: 没有被衣服或覆盖物遮住的
senses.example: He walked on the sand in bare feet.
senses.exampleCN: 他赤脚走在沙滩上。
senses.why: Bare is an old English word for 'uncovered', and the body is its most direct subject.
senses.whyCN: bare 是古英语中表示「没有遮盖」的词，身体是它最直接的对象。

senses.title: Empty or leafless
senses.definition: without leaves, furniture or other usual covering
senses.definitionCN: 没有叶子、家具或其他常见覆盖物
senses.example: The trees stood bare against the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 树木光秃秃地立在天空下。
senses.why: A surface with nothing on it is uncovered in the same way as skin, so bare describes empty branches and rooms.
senses.whyCN: 表面什么都没有，和皮肤没被遮住是同样的「空」，所以 bare 也形容光秃的树枝与空荡的房间。

senses.title: Only just enough
senses.definition: no more than the minimum needed
senses.definitionCN: 不超过所需的最低限度
senses.example: They had the bare minimum of food.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的食物仅够最低需要。
senses.why: If nothing extra covers a thing, only the essential remains, which produced the sense of a bare minimum.
senses.whyCN: 如果没有多余的东西覆盖，剩下的就只有必需部分，于是产生「最低限度」的义项。

definition_zh: 第十五；十五分之一
definition_en: coming after the fourteenth, or one of fifteen equal parts
core_image: 队伍一直排到街角，他数到第十五个才停下
scene: 队伍一直排到街角，她数到第十五个才停下。 She finished fifteenth in the race.
sceneCN: 这里 fifteenth 是「第十五」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她在比赛中获得第十五名。

senses.title: Ordinal fifteen
senses.definition: coming after the fourteenth in order
senses.definitionCN: 在顺序上位于第十四之后
senses.example: She finished fifteenth in the race.
senses.exampleCN: 她在比赛中获得第十五名。
senses.why: This is the ordering sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是表示顺序的义项。

senses.title: One of fifteen parts
senses.definition: one of fifteen equal parts of something
senses.definitionCN: 某物被均分成十五份中的一份
senses.example: He paid a fifteenth of the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 他付了费用的十五分之一。
senses.why: Ordinals also name fractions.
senses.whyCN: 序数词也可以表示分数。

items.cn: fifteoþa 意为顺序上的第十五。

items.en: The ordinal suffix marked position.

definition_zh: 愉快地；客气地；宜人地
definition_en: in a way that gives pleasure or feels agreeable; also in a polite and friendly manner
core_image: 一个人说话时声音放得很轻，眉眼松开，让旁边的人也跟着放松下来
scene: 雨后的清晨空气清透，街角面包店刚开门，暖香顺着风飘过来。 The morning air smelled pleasantly of fresh bread.
sceneCN: 这里是「令人愉快地、宜人地」（第 1 个义项）；句意为清晨的空气里带着刚出炉面包的香味，闻着很舒服。图中可辨识物件：面包篮、半开的店门、湿石板路。

derivatives.zh: pleasantly 的形容词基础形式，义为「令人愉快的」
同源动词，义为「使高兴；请」
由 pleasant 加名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「宜人；愉快」

senses.title: In a way that gives pleasure
senses.definition: in a manner or degree that feels enjoyable to the senses
senses.definitionCN: 以让感官觉得舒服的方式或程度
senses.example: The soup was pleasantly hot after the long walk in the rain.
senses.exampleCN: 在雨里走了很久之后，这碗汤热得正舒服。
senses.why: The adverb -ly turns the adjective pleasant into a description of how something happens, so it still measures a feeling of pleasure, now attached to a manner or a degree.
senses.whyCN: 副词后缀 -ly 把形容词 pleasant 变成描述「事情怎样发生」的词，所以它量的仍是愉悦感，只是这感觉现在附着在方式或程度上。

senses.title: In a polite and friendly manner
senses.definition: in a way that is courteous, easy and warm towards others
senses.definitionCN: 以有礼、随和、让人感到温暖的方式对待他人
senses.example: She answered the questions pleasantly, even when they were rude.
senses.exampleCN: 即便问题无礼，她仍客气地回答。
senses.why: Since the adjective can describe a person's manner, the adverb naturally describes how that manner is shown: the warmth moves from what someone is to how someone acts.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个形容词能形容人的举止，副词自然就形容这种举止怎样表现出来：暖意从「某人是什么样」转到「某人怎样做」。

senses.title: In an agreeable way, of conditions
senses.definition: in a way that makes surroundings or conditions comfortable and easy to bear
senses.definitionCN: 使环境或条件舒适、容易忍受地
senses.example: The evening cooled pleasantly after the heat of the day.
senses.exampleCN: 白天的暑气过后，傍晚凉得很舒服。
senses.why: Weather and surroundings do not act on purpose, yet we still use the adverb of manner: the comfort is described as if it were a gentle way of happening.
senses.whyCN: 天气与环境并非有意而为，我们却仍用这个方式副词：仿佛那种舒适本身就是事情发生的一种温和方式。

intro.en: Pleasantly is pleasant plus the native adverb ending -ly; behind it lies the same Latin verb of pleasing that gave please and pleasure.
intro.cn: pleasantly 是 pleasant 加本土副词词尾 -ly；它背后仍是那个给出 please 与 pleasure 的拉丁动词。

items.en: The verb placere meant to please or to be agreeable to someone.
items.cn: 动词 placere 意为使人高兴或令某人满意。

items.en: Its present participle placens, stem placent-, described what is pleasing.
items.cn: 它的现在分词 placens（词干 placent-）用来形容令人愉悦的东西。

items.en: French made the participle into the adjective plaisant, pleasing or charming.
items.cn: 法语把这个分词做成形容词 plaisant，意为令人愉悦的、讨喜的。

items.en: English took the adjective as pleasant and later added -ly, the native ending for manner.
items.cn: 英语把这个形容词取作 pleasant，后来又加上本土表方式的后缀 -ly。

items.en: Modern English pleasantly covers pleasant heat, pleasant manners and pleasant weather, always answering the question how.
items.cn: 现代英语的 pleasantly 覆盖舒服的热度、客气的举止与宜人的天气，始终在回答「怎样」这个问题。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the pleasant family and the adjective it comes from; the near-meaning group gathers other adverbs of agreeable manner.
note.cn: 形近组收 pleasant 词族及它所由来的形容词；近义组收其他表示愉快方式的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning giving pleasure; pleasantly adds the manner ending to it.
entries.definitionCN: 表示令人愉快的形容词；pleasantly 在它后面加了表方式的后缀。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to give pleasure or to ask politely.
entries.definitionCN: 表示使人高兴或礼貌请求的动词。

entries.definition: The noun naming the feeling of enjoyment.
The quality of being pleasant.
In a way that is pleasing and easy to accept.
entries.definitionCN: 以令人愉快、容易接受的方式。

entries.definition: In a pleasant or satisfactory way, in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 日常口语中表示以愉快或令人满意的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that causes great pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 以带来很大快乐的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that shows good manners.

normalIntro.en: The word is pleasant with -ly attached, and -ly always tells you it is describing how, not what.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词就是 pleasant 加上 -ly，而 -ly 始终提醒你：它描述的是「怎样」，不是「什么」。

normal.en: Pleasantly is pleasant plus -ly, the ending that turns an adjective into a manner adverb.
normal.cn: pleasantly 就是 pleasant 加 -ly，这个后缀把形容词变成方式副词。

normal.en: Because pleasant means giving pleasure, pleasantly means in a way that gives it.
normal.cn: 既然 pleasant 意为「给人愉悦的」，pleasantly 就是「以给人愉悦的方式」。

normal.en: It often answers how: how warm, how quiet, how someone spoke.
normal.cn: 它常回答「多……／怎样」：多暖、多静、某人怎么说话。

normal.en: The whole family returns to placere, so please, pleasant and pleasantly share one Latin source.
normal.cn: 整族词都回到 placere，所以 please、pleasant 与 pleasantly 共用一个拉丁来源。

normal.en: Pleasantly surprised is a fixed pairing: the surprise is welcome rather than shocking.
normal.cn: pleasantly surprised 是固定搭配：这份意外是受欢迎的，而不是令人震惊的。

abstract.en: Adding -ly to a feeling turns it into a style of happening, which is how English reports moods without naming them.
abstract.cn: 给一种感受加上 -ly，它就变成了事情发生的方式，英语正是靠这个办法不点名就报告情绪。

abstract.en: We say the evening cooled pleasantly, letting weather wear the clothes of human gentleness.
abstract.cn: 我们说傍晚凉得很舒服，等于让天气穿上人类温和的外衣。

abstract.en: A single ending lets one adjective describe heat, manners and silence, and that is the quiet power of adverbs of manner.
abstract.cn: 一个后缀就让同一个形容词去修饰热度、举止和寂静，这就是方式副词的隐性力量。

examples.en: The room was pleasantly cool after the hot street.
examples.cn: 从炎热的街上进来，房间凉得正舒服。

examples.en: He smiled pleasantly and held the door open.
examples.cn: 他客气地笑了笑，扶着门让我们过去。

examples.en: We were pleasantly surprised by how quiet the hotel was.
examples.cn: 旅馆竟如此安静，让我们感到惊喜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普莱增特利」——一口气顺下来，像有人轻声请你坐下，听着就舒服。

root: 拉丁语 placere（使人高兴）→ 古法语 plaisant → 英语 pleasant + 本土副词后缀 -ly → pleasantly。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「带来愉悦的方式」；义项分为愉悦的感受、客气的举止与宜人的环境。

branches.cn: 一碗热汤暖开被雨淋透的身体

branches.en: a calm answer given to a rude question
branches.cn: 面对无礼问题仍平静作答

branches.cn: 没有风也渐渐凉下来的傍晚

branches.cn: 用程度而非动作量出的舒适

branches.cn: 只属于举止的暖意

definition_en: the number 60, or the years and ages between sixty and sixty-nine

scene: 这座桥长约六十米。 The bridge is about sixty metres long.
sceneCN: 这里 sixty 是「六十」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这座桥长约六十米。

senses.title: The number sixty
senses.definition: the number equal to six times ten
senses.definitionCN: 等于六乘十的数字
senses.example: The bridge is about sixty metres long.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥长约六十米。
senses.why: This is the basic counting sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的计数义项。

senses.title: A decade
senses.definition: the years from sixty to sixty-nine in a century
senses.definitionCN: 一个世纪中从六十到六十九的年份
senses.example: The building was designed in the sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 这座建筑是六十年代设计的。
senses.why: The plural form names a period of ten years.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式表示十年的时期。

senses.title: The age range
senses.definition: the ages between sixty and sixty-nine
senses.definitionCN: 六十到六十九岁之间
senses.example: My grandfather is in his sixties.
senses.exampleCN: 我祖父六十多岁。
senses.why: The plural also names a stage of life.
senses.whyCN: 复数形式也表示人生的一个阶段。

intro.cn: sixty 是日耳曼语数字词，由 six 加表示「十个一组」的后缀构成。

items.en: Siex meant six.
items.cn: siex 意为六。

items.en: The suffix -tig meant a group of ten.

definition_zh: 一堆；堆叠；书库
definition_en: a neat pile of things, to put things in a pile, or the shelves in a library
core_image: 桌上整齐地堆着一摞书
scene: 桌上堆着一摞书。 A stack of books lay on the table.
sceneCN: 这里 stack 是「一堆」（第 1 个义项）；句意：桌上堆着一摞书。

senses.title: Neat pile
senses.definition: a neat pile of things placed on top of each other
senses.definitionCN: 一件件叠放整齐的一堆东西
senses.example: A stack of books lay on the table.
senses.exampleCN: 桌上堆着一摞书。
senses.why: This is the central physical sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最核心的物理义项。

senses.title: Put in a pile
senses.definition: to arrange things in a neat pile
senses.definitionCN: 把东西整齐地叠放起来
senses.example: Please stack the chairs after the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 会后请把椅子叠起来。
senses.why: The verb simply names the action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义就是这一动作本身。

senses.title: Library shelves
senses.definition: the shelves or area where books are stored
senses.definitionCN: 存放书籍的书架或区域
senses.example: She found the book in the stacks.
senses.exampleCN: 她在书库里找到了这本书。
senses.why: Library shelves are a long stack of books.
senses.whyCN: 图书馆书架就是一摞摞延伸的书。

intro.en: Stack comes from Old Norse stakkr, a haystack.
intro.cn: stack 来自古诺尔斯语 stakkr，意为草堆。

items.en: Stakkr meant a haystack.

items.en: Stack named a pile of hay or wood.

items.en: The sense widened to any neat pile.
items.cn: 词义扩展到任何整齐的堆。

items.en: The verb sense of piling grew later.
items.cn: 「堆叠」的动词义后来出现。

items.en: Library shelves borrowed the word.

note.en: Stack is compared with look-alike words and words for piles.

things lying on top of each other

normalIntro.en: Stack began as a haystack and now means any neat pile or the act of piling.
normalIntro.cn: stack 原指草堆，如今指任何整齐的堆或堆叠动作。

normal.en: Stack the plates here.
normal.cn: 把盘子叠在这里。

normal.en: A stack of papers filled the desk.
normal.cn: 一摞文件堆满了书桌。

normal.en: The chairs stack easily.
normal.cn: 这些椅子容易叠放。

normal.en: Smoke rose from the chimney stack.
normal.cn: 烟从烟囱里升起。

normal.en: He blew his stack at the news.
normal.cn: 听到这个消息他勃然大怒。

abstract.en: Order turns a heap into a stack.
abstract.cn: 秩序把乱堆变成整齐的一摞。

abstract.en: Each layer holds the one above.

abstract.en: A tall pile begins with one item.

dict_mnemonic.text: stack 是「一摞、堆叠」；a stack of books 是一摞书，stack up 是堆积，chimney stack 是烟囱；图书馆的 stacks 指书库。

root: 来自古诺尔斯语 stakkr（草堆），由「干草堆」扩展到任何整齐的堆，再引申出堆叠动作和图书馆书库。

sensesIntro.en: Stack means a neat pile, the act of piling, or library shelves.
sensesIntro.cn: stack 指整齐的一堆、堆叠动作，或图书馆书库。

core.en: Things laid one on top of another.
core.cn: 一件件叠放在彼此之上。

branches.en: Books rise in an even column.
branches.cn: 书本叠成整齐的一列。

branches.en: Hands lift chairs onto one another.
branches.cn: 双手把椅子一把把叠上去。

branches.en: Long shelves fill a quiet room.
branches.cn: 长长的书架填满安静的房间。

branches.en: The pile and the piling share one shape.

branches.en: Shelves are books stacked by design.

definition_zh: 理解；理解力；领悟；阅读理解练习
definition_en: the ability to understand something, or the act of understanding it
core_image: 一段外文读到最后，脑中忽然亮起整幅画面
scene: 老师让学生读完后用自己的话说出大意。 The test measures reading comprehension, not memory.
sceneCN: 这里 comprehension 指「理解」（第 1 个义项：读懂意思的过程）；句意是这项测试考的是阅读理解，而不是记忆力。

pos.zh: 理解；理解力；阅读理解练习

senses.title: The act of understanding
senses.definition: the act of understanding the meaning of something
senses.definitionCN: 理解某事物含义的过程
senses.example: The poem is beyond my comprehension.
senses.exampleCN: 这首诗超出了我的理解。
senses.why: Meaning is not heard or seen; it is grasped inside the mind.
senses.whyCN: 意思不是听到或看到的，而是在脑中 grasp 到的。

senses.title: The ability to understand
senses.definition: the ability to understand something
senses.definitionCN: 理解某事物的能力
senses.example: His comprehension of the rules improved quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 他对规则的理解力提高得很快。
senses.why: Some minds take hold of an idea faster than others, and we name that power.
senses.whyCN: 有些头脑抓住一个想法更快，我们就给这种能力命名。

senses.title: A test of understanding
senses.definition: a test that measures how well you understand a text
senses.definitionCN: 衡量你对一段文字理解程度的测试
senses.example: She scored full marks on the comprehension.
senses.exampleCN: 她在阅读理解练习中得了满分。
senses.why: Schools turned the ability into a task with questions and marks.
senses.whyCN: 学校把这种能力变成带问题和分数的任务。

intro.en: Comprehension comes from Latin comprehendere, to seize or grasp, and first named the act of taking an idea into the mind.
intro.cn: comprehension 来自拉丁语 comprehendere（抓住、握住），最初指把想法收入脑中的动作。

items.en: Com- meant together and prehendere meant to seize.
items.cn: com- 表示一起，prehendere 表示抓住。

items.en: Comprehendere described seizing something with the hand or the mind.
items.cn: comprehendere 描述用手或用心智抓住某物。

items.en: Comprehensio named a complete grasp of a subject.
items.cn: comprehensio 指对某个主题的完整把握。

items.en: Old French comprehension kept the sense of full understanding.
items.cn: 古法语 comprehension 保留了完整理解的意思。

items.en: English comprehension first meant the act of grasping meaning.
items.cn: 英语 comprehension 最初指把握含义的行为。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that share the Latin root of comprehension, and the meaning group names other words for understanding.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 comprehension 同根同形的词，近义组列出其他表示理解的词。

entries.definition: including everything that is needed
to understand something fully
easy to understand
the knowledge of how something works
a full understanding of a subject
the way you notice or understand something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a hand closing on an object, then move to the mind closing on an idea.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一只手合拢抓住东西开始，再走到心智抓住一个想法。

normal.en: Com- is together and prehend is to seize, so comprehension is the mind seizing meaning.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，prehend 是抓住，comprehension 就是心智抓住意思。

normal.en: A text you comprehend stops being a wall of marks and becomes a picture.
normal.cn: 一段你读懂的文字，会从一堵符号墙变成一幅画。

normal.en: Comprehension is the noun, comprehend is the verb, comprehensible is the adjective.
normal.cn: comprehension 是名词，comprehend 是动词，comprehensible 是形容词。

normal.en: Beyond comprehension means the hand of the mind cannot close on it.
normal.cn: beyond comprehension 意味着心智之手合不拢它。

normal.en: A comprehension test only asks whether the picture formed.
normal.cn: 阅读理解测试只问那幅画面有没有形成。

abstract.en: Picture a fist slowly closing around a small bright object.
abstract.cn: 想象一只拳头慢慢合拢，包住一个发亮的小东西。

abstract.en: Picture fog clearing to reveal a whole valley.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气散开，露出整片山谷。

abstract.en: Picture puzzle pieces clicking into one picture.
abstract.cn: 想象拼图一块块咔哒合拢成一幅画。

examples.en: The instructions are simple and within most readers' comprehension.
examples.cn: 这些说明很简单，在多数读者的理解范围之内。

examples.en: Reading aloud can improve a child's comprehension.
examples.cn: 大声朗读能提高孩子的理解力。

examples.en: He answered every comprehension question correctly.
examples.cn: 他答对了每一道阅读理解题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 comprehension 记成 com（一起）加 prehend（抓住）：把意思整个抓住，就是理解。

root: 源自拉丁语 comprehendere（com 一起 + prehendere 抓住），本义是抓住、握住，后指心智把握含义，即理解与理解力。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of grasping meaning, to the power to grasp it, and finally to the school test built on that power.
sensesIntro.cn: 从抓住含义的动作，到抓住含义的能力，最后到以这种能力为基础的学校测试。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand closing around an object, just as the mind closes around an idea.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手合拢包住东西，正如心智合拢包住一个想法。

branches.en: Understanding as an act is the oldest and most direct sense.
branches.cn: 作为动作的理解，是最古老也最直接的义项。

branches.en: The same act, seen as a lasting power, becomes an ability.
branches.cn: 同一个动作若看作持久的能力，就成了理解力。

branches.en: Schools turned the ability into a paper task.
branches.cn: 学校把这种能力变成纸面上的任务。

branches.en: Act and ability differ only in whether they happen once or often.
branches.cn: 动作与能力只差在发生一次还是经常发生。

branches.en: A test exists only because the ability can be measured.
branches.cn: 测试之所以存在，正因为这种能力可以被衡量。

intro.en: Comprehension is built on Latin com-, together, plus prehendere, to seize, with the noun ending -ion.
intro.cn: comprehension 由拉丁语 com-（一起）、prehendere（抓住）与名词词尾 -ion 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base prehend- also gives apprehend and prehensile.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基 prehend- 还给出 apprehend 与 prehensile。

items.example: Her comprehension of the text was exact.
items.exampleCN: 她对这篇文字的理解很准确。
我无法理解这样的残忍。

items.example: The guide is clear and comprehensible.
They tested the comprehensibility of the form.
items.exampleCN: 他们测试了这张表格的可理解性。

items.meaning: in a way that can be understood
items.exampleCN: 他把规则解释得很清楚。

items.example: The library has a comprehensive index.
items.exampleCN: 这家图书馆有全面的索引。

items.example: The report covers the issue comprehensively.
items.exampleCN: 这份报告全面地涵盖了该问题。
这条消息令人无法理解。

definition_zh: 不能接受的；难以忍受的；不合格的；令人不满的
definition_en: not good enough to be agreed to, tolerated, or let through
core_image: 一件东西递到门口，被守门人抬手推了回去
scene: 会议室的门口贴着一张告示，写着着装要求，短裤和拖鞋一律不许进。 Loud phone calls during the lecture are simply unacceptable.
sceneCN: 这里 unacceptable 是「不能接受的」（第 1 个义项：不足以让人同意或容许）；句意为在讲座中大声打电话简直不可接受。递来的东西被守门人推回，正是这个词的画面。

pos.zh: 形容词：不能接受的；不可容许的
形容词：不合格的；难以忍受的

derivatives.zh: 形容词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「不可接受地」
形容词加 -ability 构成名词，义为「不可接受性」
去掉否定前缀的原动词，义为「接受」

senses.title: Not able to be agreed to
senses.definition: so poor or wrong that no one can agree to it
senses.definitionCN: 太差或太错，以致无人能同意
senses.example: The terms were unacceptable to both sides.
senses.exampleCN: 这些条件双方都无法接受。
senses.why: Accept comes from Latin accipere, to receive, so unacceptable describes something the hand refuses to take.
senses.whyCN: accept 来自拉丁语 accipere（接收），因此 unacceptable 就是「拒绝接过来的东西」。

senses.title: Not to be tolerated
senses.definition: behaving in a way that a community will not put up with
senses.definitionCN: 行为方式让所在群体无法容忍
senses.example: Such rude remarks are unacceptable here.
senses.exampleCN: 这种粗鲁的话在这里是不可容忍的。
senses.why: To tolerate is to bear a weight, and what a community will not bear is by definition unacceptable.
senses.whyCN: tolerate 意为承重，一个群体不肯承起的东西，按定义就是 unacceptable。

senses.title: Below the required standard
senses.definition: falling short of the standard set for a product or a piece of work
senses.definitionCN: 未达到产品或作品所设定的标准
senses.example: The water sample was unacceptable for drinking.
senses.exampleCN: 这个水样不适合饮用。
senses.why: A receiver turns away what fails inspection, and the same word covers goods and grades.
senses.whyCN: 收货人会把检验不合格的东西退回，同一个词也覆盖货物与成绩。

senses.title: Too great to bear
senses.definition: of a risk or cost, too high to be allowed to stand
senses.definitionCN: 就风险或代价而言高到不允许存在
senses.example: The delay posed an unacceptable risk to patients.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误给病人带来了不可承受的风险。
senses.why: From a thing you will not take, the word moves to a level you will not let stand.
senses.whyCN: 从「不肯接下的东西」转到「不肯让它继续存在的程度」。

senses.title: Morally or socially offensive
senses.titleCN: 令人难以接受的；有伤风化的
senses.definition: offending the moral sense of most people
senses.definitionCN: 冒犯多数人的道德感
senses.example: The film was criticized for its unacceptable portrayal of violence.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影因对暴力的呈现令人难以接受而受到批评。
senses.why: A whole society can refuse a portrayal just as a person refuses a parcel.
senses.whyCN: 整个社会也可以像个人拒收包裹那样，拒绝一种呈现方式。

intro.en: The word is the English negative of acceptable, which comes from Latin.
intro.cn: 这个词是 acceptable 的英语否定形式，后者来自拉丁语。

items.en: Accipere joins ad-, to, and capere, to take, meaning to receive.
items.cn: accipere 由 ad-（向）与 capere（拿）组成，意为接收。

items.en: Acceptabilis is what is welcome or pleasing when received.
items.cn: acceptabilis 指接到手时令人满意的、受欢迎的东西。

items.en: Old French passes acceptable into English with the same sense of welcome.
items.cn: 古法语把 acceptable 传入英语，仍含「受欢迎」之义。

items.en: The un- negative appears as the word spreads into contracts and rules.
items.cn: 随着这个词进入契约与规则文本，un- 否定形出现了。

items.en: Modern usage makes it a standard phrase of complaint and of policy.
items.cn: 现代用法让它成为抱怨与政策文本中的常用词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the accept family, and the near-meaning group collects words of refusal and fault.
note.cn: 形近组汇集 accept 词族，近义组汇集表示拒绝与不合格的词。

entries.definition: good enough to be agreed to
the act of receiving or agreeing
not yet received or agreed to
too bad to be endured
not allowed to be considered
below the required quality
meeting the required standard

normalIntro.en: Read it as a hand at the door: un- says no, accept says take, able says can be.
normalIntro.cn: 把它读成门口的一只手：un- 说不，accept 说接，able 说能。

normal.en: Accept comes from capere, to take, so unacceptable is what will not be taken.
normal.cn: accept 源自 capere（拿），unacceptable 就是拿不下、不肯接的。

normal.en: Acceptable and unacceptable pair up as the two verdicts on a proposal.
normal.cn: acceptable 与 unacceptable 是一对判词，用来评价一项提议。

normal.en: Acceptance is the noun for taking something in; unacceptability is the quality of being refused.
normal.cn: acceptance 是接纳这一行为的名词，unacceptability 是被拒的性质。

normal.en: The adverb unacceptably often stands before high, slow, or long.
normal.cn: 副词 unacceptably 常放在 high、slow、long 前。

normal.en: Contracts use it for terms, and doctors use it for risk levels.
normal.cn: 契约里用它说条款，医生用它说风险等级。

abstract.en: See a parcel pushed back across a counter without a word.
abstract.cn: 看见一个包裹被无声地推回柜台外面。

abstract.en: Watch a doorman raise one flat palm at a badly dressed guest.
abstract.cn: 看门卫对一位穿着不当的客人竖起手掌。

abstract.en: Then feel a number on a gauge climb past the red line.
abstract.cn: 再感觉仪表上的数字爬过红线。

examples.en: The committee found the proposal unacceptable.

examples.en: The noise level at night was unacceptably high.

branches.cn: 谈判分支：条款无法被同意。

branches.cn: 行为分支：行为冒犯了群体。

branches.en: The quality branch, where a product fails the standard.

branches.en: The risk branch, where a level is too high to allow.

latinIntro.cn: capere（拿）这一词根还支撑着 capture、receive、except 等词。

definition_zh: 分离；分隔；分居；分工
definition_en: the act of dividing or being apart, a boundary between things, or a legal arrangement of living apart
core_image: 一道半透明的隔板立在房间中央，两边的人各自忙碌
scene: 这对夫妻在分居一年后离婚了。 The couple divorced after a year of separation.
sceneCN: 这里 separation 是「分居」（第 3 个义项）；句意：这对夫妻在分居一年后离婚了。

senses.title: Act of dividing
senses.definition: the act of moving things or people apart
senses.definitionCN: 把人或物分开的动作
senses.example: The separation of the twins was difficult.
senses.exampleCN: 把这对双胞胎分开很困难。
senses.why: This is the basic noun sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是基本的名词义。

senses.title: Boundary
senses.definition: a line or space that keeps things apart
senses.definitionCN: 使事物保持分开的界线或间隔
senses.example: A thin wall provides separation between the rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 一堵薄墙把两个房间隔开。
senses.why: A dividing line is also a separation.
senses.whyCN: 分隔线本身也是一种分离。

senses.title: Living apart
senses.definition: a legal arrangement in which a couple lives apart
senses.definitionCN: 夫妻合法分开居住的安排
senses.example: The couple divorced after a year of separation.
senses.exampleCN: 这对夫妻在分居一年后离婚了。
senses.why: The general sense narrows to marriage.
senses.whyCN: 一般义缩小到婚姻关系。

senses.title: Division of work
senses.definition: the dividing of work among people
senses.definitionCN: 把工作在人们之间分开
senses.example: Clear separation of duties prevents mistakes.
senses.exampleCN: 明确的职责分工能防止错误。
senses.why: Tasks can be separated as well as objects.
senses.whyCN: 任务也能像物体一样被分开。

intro.en: Separation comes from Latin separatio, a setting apart, from separare.
intro.cn: separation 出自拉丁语 separatio（分开），源于 separare（使分开）。

items.en: Separare meant to set apart.
items.cn: separare 意为使分开。

items.en: Separation named the act of dividing.
items.cn: separatio 指分开的行为。

items.en: Old French separation kept the noun.
items.cn: 古法语 separation 保留了这个名词。

items.en: English separation covered both space and marriage.
items.cn: 英语 separation 兼指空间与婚姻。

items.en: It also names the division of powers and duties.
items.cn: 它也指权力与职责的分立。

note.en: Separation is compared with similar-looking words and with words for division.
note.cn: 把 separation 与形近词以及表示分割的词作比较。

entries.definition: to divide
in separate ways
a supporter of separation
the act of splitting
a break or division
an empty space between things

normalIntro.en: Separation is the act or state of being apart, in space, marriage, or work.
normalIntro.cn: separation 是分开的行为或状态，可指空间、婚姻或工作。

normal.en: Separation ends in -tion, naming an action.
normal.cn: separation 以 -tion 结尾，表示动作。

normal.en: A wall can create separation.
normal.cn: 一堵墙可以形成分隔。

normal.en: Legal separation is not divorce.
normal.cn: 合法分居并不等于离婚。

normal.en: Separation of powers divides government.
normal.cn: 权力分立把政府职权分开。

normal.en: Separation anxiety is fear of being apart.
normal.cn: 分离焦虑是害怕分开。

abstract.en: Every boundary is a decision about what to keep apart.
abstract.cn: 每条界线都是关于什么该分开的决定。

abstract.en: Distance can protect what closeness would break.
abstract.cn: 距离能保护亲密会破坏的东西。

abstract.en: Dividing work well can unite a team.
abstract.cn: 把工作分好，反而能团结一个团队。

examples.en: The couple divorced after a year of separation.
examples.cn: 这对夫妻在分居一年后离婚了。
