examples.en: Clear separation of duties prevents mistakes.
examples.cn: 明确的职责分工能防止错误。

dict_mnemonic.text: separation 由 separate（分开）加 -ion 构成，出自拉丁语 separatio，本义「分开的行为」，后指分隔、分居与分工。

root: 源自拉丁语 separatio（分开），由 separare（使分开）加名词后缀构成，核心义「分开的状态或行为」。

sensesIntro.en: Separation means the act of dividing, a boundary, living apart, or the division of work.
sensesIntro.cn: separation 意为分离、分隔、分居或分工。

core.en: The act or state of being set apart.
core.cn: 被分开的行为或状态。

branches.en: Moving people or things apart.
branches.cn: 把人或物分开。

branches.en: A line or wall between spaces.
branches.cn: 空间之间的线或墙。

branches.en: A couple living apart by agreement.
branches.cn: 夫妻依约分开居住。

branches.en: Work divided among people.
branches.cn: 在人们之间分配的工作。

branches.en: Physical and legal distance share a name.
branches.cn: 物理距离与法律距离共用一个名称。

intro.en: Separation belongs to the Latin separare family.
intro.cn: separation 属于拉丁语 separare（使分开）词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin separatio and separare are the historical base.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 separatio 与 separare 是历史词根。

items.exampleCN: 分离主义分裂了这个地区。

definition_zh: 严格地；完全地
definition_en: in a way that demands rules be followed, or completely and exactly
core_image: 一条画得笔直的界线，谁也不能踩过去
scene: 这里严格禁止吸烟。 Smoking is strictly forbidden here.
sceneCN: 这里 strictly 是「严格地」（第 1 个义项）；句意：这里严格禁止吸烟。

senses.title: According to rules
senses.definition: in a way that insists rules are obeyed
senses.definitionCN: 以要求遵守规定的方式
senses.example: Smoking is strictly forbidden here.
senses.exampleCN: 这里严格禁止吸烟。
senses.why: This keeps the rule tight.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项把规定绷得很紧。

senses.title: Completely
senses.definition: completely, or in the exact sense
senses.definitionCN: 完全地，或就确切意义而言
senses.example: Strictly speaking, the answer is wrong.
senses.exampleCN: 严格来说，这个答案是错的。
senses.why: The rule of exactness now applies to words.
senses.whyCN: 精确的规则在这里用到了措辞上。

intro.en: Strictly is strict plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: strictly 由 strict 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Strictus meant drawn tight.
items.cn: strictus 意为拉紧的。

items.en: Strict described tight control.
items.cn: strict 描写紧密的控制。

items.en: Strictly described acting by the rules.
items.cn: strictly 描写按规矩行事。

items.en: Strictly speaking marked exact meaning.
items.cn: strictly speaking 标出确切含义。

items.en: It also strengthened words like forbidden.
items.cn: 它也用来加强 forbidden 这类词。

note.en: Strictly is compared with look-alike words and with words for complete degree.
note.cn: 把 strictly 与形近词以及表示完全程度的词作比较。

entries.definition: demanding obedience
in a direct line
a plan for success
in a harsh way
with complete accuracy
completely

normalIntro.en: Strictly holds the line, whether of a rule or of a meaning.
normalIntro.cn: strictly 把线拉紧，不管是规定的线还是词义的线。

normal.en: Photography is strictly prohibited.
normal.cn: 严禁拍照。

normal.en: This information is strictly confidential.
normal.cn: 这条信息是绝密的。

normal.en: Strictly speaking, he is not wrong.
normal.cn: 严格来说，他没错。

normal.en: Use it only when strictly necessary.
normal.cn: 只在绝对必要时使用。

normal.en: Numbers are strictly limited.
normal.cn: 人数受到严格限制。

abstract.en: A strict line is easy to see and hard to cross.
abstract.cn: 严格的线，看得清，也难越过。

abstract.en: Strictly speaking is honesty with a ruler.
abstract.cn: 严格来说，是拿着尺子的诚实。

abstract.en: Some doors are strictly one way.
abstract.cn: 有些门，严格来说只有一个方向。

examples.en: Smoking is strictly forbidden here.
examples.cn: 这里严格禁止吸烟。

examples.en: Strictly speaking, the answer is wrong.
examples.cn: 严格来说，这个答案是错的。

examples.en: This information is strictly confidential.
examples.cn: 这条信息是绝密的。

dict_mnemonic.text: strictly 是 strict 加 -ly；按规定办事是严格地，把话说得一点不含糊是完全地、确切地，如 strictly speaking。

root: 由 strict（严格的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；strict 源自拉丁语 strictus（拉紧的），因此 strictly 的核心是「不留松动地」。

sensesIntro.en: Strictly can mean by the rules, or in the exact and complete sense.
sensesIntro.cn: strictly 可以是按规定地，也可以是确切而完全地。

core.en: A line drawn once, not to be redrawn.
core.cn: 一条画定就不再改的线。

branches.en: A sign says no entry.
branches.cn: 牌子上写着禁止入内。

branches.en: A word is read at its exact value.
branches.cn: 一个词按它确切的意思来读。

branches.en: A guard checks every pass.
branches.cn: 守卫检查每一张通行证。

branches.en: A strict rule and an exact reading both refuse slack.
branches.cn: 严格的规定与确切的读法，都不接受松动。

branches.en: Strictly speaking admits the letter, not the spirit.
branches.cn: 严格来说，只认字面，不认精神。

intro.en: Strictly is built from strict and forms no further endings.
intro.cn: strictly 由 strict 构成，本身不再加词尾。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is strictus, drawn tight.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 strictus，意为拉紧的。

items.example: Strictly speaking, it is a fruit.

definition_zh: 本能；直觉；天性
definition_en: a natural ability or urge to behave in a certain way without being taught
core_image: 雏鸟在蛋壳刚裂开时，就朝着光的方向伸出脖子
scene: 海边沙滩上，刚出壳的小龟没有谁教，直接朝海浪爬去。 Birds find their way home by instinct, not by memory.
sceneCN: 这里 instinct 是「本能」（第 1 个义项：无需学习的天生行为能力或倾向），句意是鸟靠本能而非记忆找到回家的路。画面里能看到的物件：蛋壳、沙滩、海浪、光。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加 -ive 构成，义为「本能的；直觉的」
由 instinctive 加 -ly 构成，义为「本能地」
由本词加 -ual 构成，义为「本能的」，多用于心理 学

senses.title: A natural urge
senses.definition: a natural tendency to act in a particular way, present from birth and not learned
senses.definitionCN: 从出生起就有、并非学来的行为倾向
senses.example: A cat has an instinct to hide its waste.
senses.exampleCN: 猫有掩埋粪便的本能。
senses.why: Latin instinctus was an inner impulse; the word kept that image of something urging from inside.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 instinctus 指内在冲动；这个词保留了「体内有东西在催促」的意象。

senses.title: A gut feeling
senses.definition: a feeling about what is right or dangerous, felt before any reasoning
senses.definitionCN: 在推理之前就对对错或危险产生的感觉
senses.example: My instinct told me not to sign the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 我的直觉告诉我不要签这份文件。
senses.why: The inner urge is felt as knowledge: the same push now warns rather than drives.
senses.whyCN: 内在的驱使被感受为一种认识：同一股推力如今是在警告，而不是在驱动。

senses.title: A natural talent
senses.definition: a natural ability for something that seems to come without training
senses.definitionCN: 看似无需训练就有的能力
senses.example: She has an instinct for finding good stories.
senses.exampleCN: 她天生善于发现好故事。
senses.why: When the natural push meets a kind of work, it looks like talent rather than urge.
senses.whyCN: 当这股天生的推力遇上某类工作时，它看起来像天赋而不像冲动。

intro.en: Instinct is a Latin noun from instinguere "to prick or urge on", pictured as an inner goad.
intro.cn: instinct 来自拉丁语 instinguere「刺、驱使」的名词形式，意象是体内有一根刺在催动。

items.en: Stinguere meant to prick or goad, related to the mark or point of a sting.
items.cn: stinguere 意为「刺、驱使」，与刺点、刺痕有关。

items.en: In- plus stinguere gave instinguere, "to urge on from within".
items.cn: in- 加 stinguere 得到 instinguere，意为「从内部驱使」。

items.en: The noun instinctus meant an impulse or inspiration.
items.cn: 名词 instinctus 意为「冲动、灵感」。

items.en: In the seventeenth century it was applied to the behaviour of animals.
items.cn: 十七世纪起用于描述动物的行为。

items.en: Psychology later extended it to human urges and untaught reactions.
items.cn: 后来的心理学把它扩展到人的冲动与未经学习的反应。

note.en: The look-alike group looks and sounds like instinct; the near-meaning group holds other words for untaught knowledge.
note.cn: 形近组在外形和读音上接近 instinct；近义组收其他表示「未学而知」的词。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning done without thinking.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「本能的」，指不经思考就做。

entries.definition: Clearly separate; the same looking ending, a different Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「截然不同的」，词尾相似但拉丁动词不同。

entries.definition: No longer existing, literally "stung out".
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「灭绝的」，字面是「被熄灭的」。

entries.definition: Knowledge felt without reasons, close to gut feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「直觉」，指没有理由的感觉。

entries.definition: A sudden wish to act, often short-lived.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「冲动」，常是短暂的。

entries.definition: An automatic bodily reaction, narrower than instinct.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「反射」，范围比 instinct 窄。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the image of an inner goad and the phrase by instinct.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子利用「体内有刺在催」的意象，以及短语 by instinct。

normal.en: in plus sting: an instinct is a sting inside that makes you act.
normal.cn: in 加 sting：instinct 就是体内的一根刺，催你行动。

normal.en: Act by instinct; learn by practice.
normal.cn: 本能让你行动，练习让你学会。

normal.en: Trust your instincts when there is no time to think.
normal.cn: 没时间思考时就相信直觉。

normal.en: Instinct is not the same as memory.
normal.cn: 本能不等于记忆。

normal.en: Instinctive is the adjective; instinctively is the adverb.
normal.cn: instinctive 是形容词，instinctively 是副词。

abstract.en: A newborn turtle runs to the sea with nobody teaching it.
abstract.cn: 刚出生的小龟无人教就爬向大海。

abstract.en: Instinct is wisdom stored in the body before the mind.
abstract.cn: 本能是心灵之前就存进身体的智慧。

abstract.en: Reason can explain what instinct decided first.
abstract.cn: 理性只能解释本能先做出的决定。

examples.en: He dived into the water by instinct.
examples.cn: 他本能地跳进水里。

examples.en: Her instinct was to say nothing.
examples.cn: 她的直觉是保持沉默。

examples.en: Birds follow the instinct to fly south in autumn.
examples.cn: 秋天鸟儿依照本能南飞。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「因斯汀克」——因为身上像被刺了一下，就本能地躲开

root: 拉丁语 stinguere「刺、点燃」→ in- + stinguere = instinguere「从内部驱使」→ 名词 instinctus「冲动、灵感」→ 十六世纪英语；十七世纪起用于动物行为，后扩展至人的直觉。

sensesIntro.en: Three senses: a natural urge, a gut feeling, and an untaught talent.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项：天生冲动、直觉感觉，以及未经训练的天赋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a newly hatched bird stretches towards the light before it can walk.
core.cn: 核心意象：刚出壳的雏鸟还不会走，就朝光伸出脖子。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: behaviour that arrives with birth.
branches.cn: 动物这条线：与生俱来的行为。

branches.en: THE MOMENT OF CHOICE: a feeling before reasoning.
branches.cn: 抉择这条线：推理之前的感觉。

branches.en: THE STORYTELLER: a natural knack for a kind of work.
branches.cn: 讲故事的人这条线：某一类工作的天然本领。

branches.en: THE LINK: both are untaught and quick, one about action and one about judgement.
branches.cn: 连接线：两者都未经教导且迅速，一个关乎行动，一个关乎判断。

branches.en: THE SPREAD: the talent sense is looser and more social.
branches.cn: 扩展线：「天赋」义更宽松、更社会性。

intro.en: Instinct is in- "in" plus the Latin root stingu- "prick", with the noun form of the participle.
intro.cn: instinct 是 in-「在内」加拉丁词根 stingu-「刺」，采用分词式的名词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin instinguere and instinctus are attested; the deeper origin of stinguere is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 instinguere 与 instinctus 均有记载，stinguere 的更早来源并不确定。

items.example: It places the goad inside the creature.
items.exampleCN: 它把这根刺放在生物体内。

items.example: The root also appears in extinct.
The verb is the direct source.
It gives the noun its compact form.

items.exampleCN: instinctive 意为受本能驱动的。

definition_zh: 崇拜；敬仰；礼拜；做礼拜
definition_en: to show deep respect and love for a god, or to admire someone greatly; also the act or service of such respect
core_image: 一个人弯下腰去，额头几乎触到地面
scene: 老庙的门槛被几代人的膝盖磨得凹下去一块。 Every morning the villagers come to worship at the small shrine by the river.
sceneCN: 这里 worship 是「崇拜、敬拜」（第 1 个义项：对神或极受敬重者表达深深的敬意）；句意为每天早晨村民们都到河边那座小庙里敬拜。弯腰到额头几乎触地的姿态，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 由 worship 加 -er 构成，义为「崇拜者；礼拜者」
由 worship 加 -ful 构成，义为「恭敬的；崇拜的」
由 worshipful 加 -ly 构成，义为「恭敬地」

senses.title: Reverence for a god
senses.definition: to give a god the highest honour with prayer and ritual
senses.definitionCN: 以祈祷与仪式给神灵最高的敬意
senses.example: Every morning the villagers come to worship at the small shrine by the river.
senses.exampleCN: 每天早晨村民们到河边那座小庙里敬拜。
senses.why: The compound said worth-ship, the state of being worthy, and its highest form was honour paid to a god.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词原说 worth-ship（有价值、配得尊敬的状态），其最高形式就是对神的敬意。

senses.title: Deep admiration for a person
senses.definition: to admire someone so much that one almost overlooks their faults
senses.definitionCN: 极其钦佩某人，几乎看不到其缺点
senses.example: The young players worship the old coach who trained them.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻球员们非常崇拜训练他们的老教练。
senses.why: Because the word names deserved honour rather than only divine honour, it fits a person who has earned respect.
senses.whyCN: 这个词指应得的敬意而不只是对神的敬意，所以也能用于赢得尊重的人。

senses.title: The service itself
senses.definition: the religious ceremony at which such honour is given
senses.definitionCN: 举行这种敬意仪式的宗教活动
senses.example: The church holds worship at ten on Sunday mornings.
senses.exampleCN: 这所教堂周日上午十点举行礼拜。
senses.why: The state of honouring turns into the gathering where it happens, so the noun names an event.
senses.whyCN: 敬奉的状态变成了举行敬奉的聚会，于是名词也指一场活动。

senses.title: To be treated with such honour
senses.definition: to be the one before whom others bow, said of a place or an image
senses.definitionCN: 被人俯身敬奉的对象，就地点或圣像而言
senses.example: The old stone figure was worshipped long before the village had a name.
senses.exampleCN: 那座古老石像受敬奉的年代，远比村子有名字要早。
senses.why: The verb turns round: the one who receives the bowing is now the subject of the passive form.
senses.whyCN: 动词转了向：接受敬拜的一方，成了被动形式的主语。

intro.en: Worship is Old English weorthscipe, worth-ship, the condition of being worthy of honour, and only later the honour paid to God.
intro.cn: worship 来自古英语 weorthscipe，即 worth-ship，意为「配得尊敬的状态」，后来才指对神的敬奉。

items.en: weorthscipe joined weorth, worth, with scipe, a state or condition.
items.cn: weorthscipe 由 weorth（值得）与 scipe（状态）复合。

items.en: In early use it named the honour that a worthy person deserved.
items.cn: 早期用法指可敬之人应得的尊敬。

items.en: The spelling shortened to worship, and the suffix -ship kept its meaning.
items.cn: 拼写缩短为 worship，后缀 -ship 保留原意。

items.en: Religious use became dominant, so the word now means honour given to a god.
items.cn: 宗教用法占据主导，如今这个词指对神的敬意。

items.en: A title, as in Your Worship, still carries the old sense of deserved honour.
items.cn: 「Your Worship」这样的称呼仍带着「应得的尊敬」这一旧义。

note.en: The first group holds the word's own forms, the second holds other words for honour and religious service.
note.cn: 第一组收这个词自己的形式，第二组收其他表示敬意与宗教仪式的词。

entries.definition: A person who worships.
Full of respect, now formal.
Third person singular.
To love or respect deeply.
To respect with something like awe.
To speak to a god in words.

normalIntro.en: Worship is worth plus ship, the suffix that names a condition, as in friendship.
normalIntro.cn: worship 是 worth 加 ship，这个后缀表示状态，如 friendship。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the p before a vowel ending: worshipped.
normal.cn: 英式拼写在元音词尾前双写 p：worshipped。

normal.en: Worship is the noun and the verb at once, so only position tells them apart.
normal.cn: worship 同时是名词和动词，只靠位置区分。

normal.en: The suffix -ship is the same one in friendship and hardship.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ship 与 friendship、hardship 里的是同一个。

normal.en: Keep the r in the middle: worship is not warship, a naval vessel.
normal.cn: 中间保留 r：worship 不是 warship（军舰）。

normal.en: A place of worship is simply a building where people pray.
normal.cn: a place of worship 就是人们祈祷的建筑。

abstract.en: A threshold worn into a hollow by generations of knees.
abstract.cn: 门槛被几代人跪出凹陷。

abstract.en: A body bending until the forehead nearly touches stone.
abstract.cn: 身体弯下去，额头几乎触到石头。

abstract.en: A name said softly, as if it might break.
abstract.cn: 一个说得很轻的名字，仿佛一用力就会碎。

examples.en: People of many faiths worship in that old building.
examples.cn: 许多信仰的人都在那座老建筑里礼拜。

examples.en: Children often worship a teacher who treats them fairly.
examples.cn: 孩子常常特别崇敬公正对待他们的老师。

examples.en: The temple has been a place of worship for six hundred years.
examples.cn: 这座寺庙作为礼拜场所已有六百年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「我惜」——心里珍重到「我惜」二字的程度，就是崇拜。

root: 古英语 weorthscipe = weorth（值得、可贵）+ scipe（状态），原义「配得尊敬的状态」，后专指对神的敬奉。

sensesIntro.en: Deserved honour comes first, then the honour given to a god, then to a person, then the ceremony, and finally the one so honoured.
sensesIntro.cn: 先是应得的尊敬，再是对神的敬奉，接着是对人的崇敬，然后是仪式本身，最后是被敬奉者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body bending until the forehead nearly touches stone.
core.cn: 核心意象：弯到额头几乎触地的身体。

branches.en: The god branch: villagers at a riverside shrine.
branches.cn: 神灵分支：河边小庙里的村民。

branches.en: The person branch: players admiring an old coach.
branches.cn: 人分支：球员崇敬老教练。

branches.en: The service branch: ten o'clock worship on Sunday.
branches.cn: 仪式分支：周日十点的礼拜。

branches.en: The image branch: a stone figure honoured before the village had a name.
branches.cn: 圣像分支：村子未得名时已受敬奉的石像。

branches.en: The degree branch: the same word for a god and for a teacher.
branches.cn: 程度分支：对神与对老师用同一个词。

intro.en: Worship was built from two native parts, worth and -ship, and it still carries the colour of deserving.
intro.cn: worship 由两个本土成分构成：worth 与 -ship，至今仍带着「配得上」的意味。

latinIntro.en: Neither part is Latin; the Latin words below name devotion from another tradition.
latinIntro.cn: 两个成分都不是拉丁语；下面的拉丁词从另一传统来指虔敬。

items.example: It says what makes a person honoured.
It forms worship, as in friendship.
items.exampleCN: 它构成 worship，如 friendship 里的 -ship。

items.example: It shares the same letters at the start.
Warship is the one with an a.

definition_zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的
definition_en: stiff and unable to bend, or strict and unwilling to change
core_image: 一根弯不动的旧金属管
scene: 这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。 The old pipe had become rigid and cracked when bent.
sceneCN: 这里 rigid 是「僵硬的」（第 1 个义项：坚硬而无法弯曲）；句意：这根旧管子已经变得僵硬，轻轻一弯就裂开了。

pos.zh: 坚硬的；僵硬的；严格的；死板的

senses.title: Stiff to the touch
senses.definition: hard and not able to bend
senses.definitionCN: 坚硬且不能弯曲
senses.example: The frame is made of rigid steel.
senses.exampleCN: 框架由坚硬的钢材制成。
senses.why: Rigid begins as the Latin word for stiff.
senses.whyCN: rigid 最初就是拉丁语中表示僵硬的那个词。

senses.title: Strict and fixed
senses.definition: not allowing change or flexibility
senses.definitionCN: 不允许改变或变通
senses.example: The school has rigid rules about phones.
senses.exampleCN: 学校对手机有严格的规定。
senses.why: A rule that cannot bend is rigid.
senses.whyCN: 不能变通的规则就是僵硬的。

senses.title: Frozen with feeling
senses.definition: unable to move because of fear or shock
senses.definitionCN: 因恐惧或震惊而无法动弹
senses.example: He stood rigid at the edge of the cliff.
senses.exampleCN: 他僵立在悬崖边。
senses.why: The body turns stiff when terror takes over.
senses.whyCN: 恐惧占据身心时，身体会变得僵硬。

intro.en: Rigid comes from Latin rigidus, stiff, from rigere, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 源自拉丁语 rigidus（僵硬），来自 rigere（变硬）。

items.en: Rigere means to be stiff.
items.cn: rigere 意为僵硬。

items.en: Rigidus means stiff or unbending.
items.cn: rigidus 意为僵硬、不弯。

items.en: French rigide keeps the physical sense.
items.cn: 法语 rigide 保留了物理含义。

items.en: English rigid adds the sense of strict rules.
items.cn: 英语 rigid 增加了严格规则的含义。

items.en: It also describes a body frozen by fear.
items.cn: 它也形容因恐惧而僵住的身体。

note.en: Rigid is stiff in body or rule; strict is firm about rules only.
note.cn: rigid 可指身体或规则僵硬，strict 只强调规则严格。

entries.definition: stiffness
in a stiff way
the state of being rigid
not easy to bend
demanding obedience
not willing to change

normalIntro.en: Rigid is a rod that refuses to bend.
normalIntro.cn: rigid 就是一根拒绝弯曲的杆子。

normal.en: Rigid rules leave no room to bend.
normal.cn: rigid rules 不留变通余地。

normal.en: A rigid frame holds its shape.
normal.cn: rigid frame 保持自身形状。

normal.en: Rigid material does not fold.
normal.cn: rigid material 不会折叠。

normal.en: Rigid with fear means frozen still.
normal.cn: rigid with fear 意为吓得僵住。

normal.en: Rigidity is the noun of rigid.
normal.cn: rigidity 是 rigid 的名词形式。

abstract.en: Picture a steel bar under heavy load.
abstract.cn: 想象一根承重的钢条。

abstract.en: Imagine a soldier standing without a twitch.
abstract.cn: 想象一名士兵一动不动地站着。

abstract.en: Think of a frozen branch snapping in wind.
abstract.cn: 想象冻硬的树枝在风中折断。

examples.en: The tent poles are light but rigid.
examples.cn: 帐篷杆又轻又硬。

examples.en: His rigid attitude made talk difficult.
examples.cn: 他死板的态度让谈话很难进行。

examples.en: She sat rigid with shock.
examples.cn: 她震惊得僵坐在那里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rigid」听起来像「硬紧的」——又硬又紧，弯都弯不动。

root: 拉丁语 rigere（变硬）→ rigidus（僵硬的）→ rigid，核心义「硬得无法弯曲，因而不能变通」。

sensesIntro.en: Rigid means physically stiff, strictly fixed, or frozen by strong feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: rigid 意为物理上僵硬、规则上严格固定，或因强烈情绪而僵住。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rod that will not bend.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根弯不动的杆子。

branches.en: Physical stiffness is the root sense.
branches.cn: 物理僵硬是根本义项。

branches.en: A rule that cannot bend becomes rigid.
branches.cn: 不能变通的规则变得僵死。

branches.en: Fear freezes the body into stiffness.
branches.cn: 恐惧把身体冻得僵硬。

branches.en: Stiff steel and stiff rules share one image.
branches.cn: 坚硬的钢与僵硬的规则共享同一个意象。

branches.en: Metal and muscles both lose their give.
branches.cn: 金属与肌肉都失去了弹性。

intro.en: Rigid comes from the Latin root rig, to be stiff.
intro.cn: rigid 来自拉丁词根 rig（僵硬）。

latinIntro.en: Rigere gives rigidus, and French rigide carries it to English.
latinIntro.cn: rigere 给出 rigidus，法语 rigide 把它带入英语。

items.example: Rig carries the idea of stiffness.

latinEntries.example: Rigidus is the source of rigid.
latinEntries.exampleCN: rigidus 是 rigid 的来源。
